; Scripted zone trigger by room+position table ($B073)
;
; Used by the routine at #R$A3E1.
;
; .
;
; Checks the hero's position against a small table of room+position hotspots
; and fires a one-shot scripted event when they step into one.
c$B03B LD B,$03      ; B=3 entries
 $B03D LD HL,$B073   ; HL=$B073 (hotspot table)
 $B040 LD A,($5C01)  ; get Current room number
*$B043 CP (HL)       ; {room matches entry?
 $B044 JR Z,$B050    ; }
 $B046 INC HL        ; next entry (stride 3)
 $B047 INC HL        ;
 $B048 INC HL        ;
 $B049 DJNZ $B043    ; loop
*$B04B XOR A         ; {no match: clear one-shot flag ($B072)
 $B04C LD ($B072),A  ; }
 $B04F RET           ;
*$B050 INC HL        ;
 $B051 LD A,(IX+$01) ; {player Y matches entry?
 $B054 CP (HL)       ; }
 $B055 JR NZ,$B04B   ;
 $B057 INC HL        ;
 $B058 LD C,(HL)     ; {C = entry X threshold
 $B059 LD A,(IX+$00) ; }
 $B05C CP C          ; {player X below it? skip
 $B05D JR C,$B04B    ; }
 $B05F PUSH AF       ;
 $B060 LD A,C        ; {C = threshold + 8
 $B061 ADD A,$08     ; }
 $B063 LD C,A        ; keep it
 $B064 POP AF        ;
 $B065 CP C          ; {player X past it? skip
 $B066 JR NC,$B04B   ; }
 $B068 LD A,($B072)  ; {already triggered ($B072)?
 $B06B OR A          ; }
 $B06C RET NZ        ;
 $B06D LD A,$16      ; status=$16
 $B06F JP $AE85      ; Set hero status ($5C06), clear hazard timer ($5C07)

; Multi-stage animation sequence, dispatched by stage counter ($5C41)
;
; .
;
; .
;
; A scripted, one-shot fanfare animation for a fixed object, played out over
; several stages as fields of it step toward target values, with a sound effect
; at each stage change. Most likely the room-$28 warp fanfare set up by
; #R$B6EE, not everyday gameplay logic.
c$B0B6 LD IY,$5B08     ; IY=object ($5B08)
 $B0BA LD HL,$5C41     ; HL=stage counter ($5C41)
 $B0BD LD A,(HL)       ;

 $B0BF JR NZ,$B104     ; }
 $B0C1 INC (HL)        ; counter++ (advance to stage 1)
 $B0C2 LD (IY+$00),$A2 ;
 $B0C6 LD (IY+$01),$04 ;
 $B0CA LD (IY+$02),$75 ;
 $B0CE LD (IY+$04),$89 ;
 $B0D2 LD (IY+$05),$68 ;
 $B0D6 LD (IY+$06),$72 ;
 $B0DA LD (IY+$07),$00 ;
 $B0DE LD (IY+$08),$71 ;
 $B0E2 LD (IY+$09),$68 ;
 $B0E6 LD (IY+$0A),$71 ;
 $B0EA LD (IY+$0B),$00 ;
 $B0EE LD A,($5BFE)    ; {completion flag ($5BFE) set? else RET
 $B0F1 OR A            ; }
 $B0F2 RET Z           ;
 $B0F3 LD (IY+$0C),$89 ;
 $B0F7 LD (IY+$0D),$5C ;
 $B0FB LD (IY+$0E),$6F ;
 $B0FF LD (IY+$0F),$00 ;
 $B103 RET             ;
*$B104 DEC A           ; {stage 1 check
 $B105 JR NZ,$B12E     ; }
 $B107 DEC (IY+$00)    ;
 $B10A LD A,(IY+$01)   ;
 $B10D ADD A,$04       ;
 $B10F LD (IY+$01),A   ;
 $B112 CP $54          ; {target $54 reached?
 $B114 RET NZ          ; }
 $B115 INC (HL)        ;
 $B116 LD A,($5BFE)    ; {completion flag set? pick branch
 $B119 OR A            ; }
 $B11A JR Z,$B125      ;
 $B11C INC (HL)        ;
 $B11D INC (IY+$0E)    ;
 $B120 LD A,$02        ;
 $B122 JP $C4B2        ; => Sound-effect dispatcher wrapper
*$B125 LD (IY+$06),$76 ;
 $B129 LD (IY+$02),$7F ;
 $B12D RET             ;
*$B12E DEC A           ; {stage 2 check
 $B12F JR NZ,$B143     ; }
 $B131 LD A,(IY+$06)   ; {field reached target $77?
 $B134 CP $77          ; }
 $B136 JR Z,$B13C      ;
 $B138 INC (IY+$06)    ;
 $B13B RET             ;
*$B13C INC (HL)        ;
 $B13D INC (HL)        ;
 $B13E LD A,$01        ;
 $B140 JP $C4B2        ; => Sound-effect dispatcher wrapper
*$B143 DEC A           ; {stage 3 check
 $B144 JR NZ,$B15D     ; }
 $B146 DEC (IY+$01)    ;
 $B149 LD A,(IY+$00)   ;
 $B14C SUB $04         ;
 $B14E LD (IY+$00),A   ;
 $B151 CP $04          ; {target <4 reached?
 $B153 RET NC          ; }
 $B154 LD (IY+$02),$7F ;
 $B158 DEC (IY+$0E)    ;
 $B15B INC (HL)        ;
 $B15C RET             ;
*$B15D INC (HL)        ; advance the sub-stage
 $B15E RET P           ; not finished? RET
 $B15F LD A,$01        ;
 $B161 LD ($5BFF),A    ; set Game-over flag
 $B164 RET             ;

; Scripted event: trigger room $1C lift sequence at a fixed spot
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Stage-0 checks the flag byte at $5C40 (via #R$B165) then initializes an
; object at $5B10 from a template; once room $5B98=2 and the hero stands at the
; fixed spot (X=$DC, Y=$48), advances the stage and fires status $1C via
; #R$AE85 (the room $1C lift trigger seen elsewhere in the room-format notes).
; Stages 1+ (dispatched at $B3AB) drive whatever animation follows - not
; detailed here, but the pattern matches the other staged-object routines
; ($B0B6, $B4E2). Reads as one of several similar "walk to this exact spot in
; this exact room to trigger a scripted lift/sequence" set-pieces.
c$B370 CALL $B165      ; Read/test flag
 $B373 RET NZ          ;
 $B374 LD IY,$5B10     ;
 $B378 LD HL,$5C41     ;
 $B37B LD A,(HL)       ;
 $B37C OR A            ; {stage 0?
 $B37D JR NZ,$B3AB     ; }
 $B37F LD (IY+$00),$64 ; init object position/frame
 $B383 LD (IY+$01),$48 ;
 $B387 LD (IY+$02),$4F ;
 $B38B LD (IY+$03),$00 ;
 $B38F LD A,($5B98)    ;
 $B392 CP $02          ; {room-category == 2?
 $B394 RET NZ          ; }
 $B395 LD A,($5B04)    ;
 $B398 CP $DC          ; {player X == $DC?
 $B39A RET NZ          ; }
 $B39B LD A,($5B05)    ;
 $B39E CP $48          ; {player Y == $48?
 $B3A0 RET NZ          ; }
 $B3A1 INC (HL)        ;
 $B3A2 RES 7,(IX+$03)  ;
 $B3A6 LD A,$1C        ; status=$1C
 $B3A8 JP $AE85        ; Set hero status ($5C06), clear hazard timer ($5C07)
*$B3AB LD A,(HL)       ; {A = stage
 $B3AC DEC A           ; }
 $B3AD JR NZ,$B3C7     ; stage 1?
 $B3AF LD A,(IX+$02)   ;
 $B3B2 CP $3E          ; {hero frame == $3E (lift ready)?
 $B3B4 RET NZ          ; }
 $B3B5 INC (HL)        ;
 $B3B6 LD (IY+$04),$C8 ;
 $B3BA LD (IY+$05),$39 ;
 $B3BE LD (IY+$06),$39 ;
 $B3C2 LD (IY+$07),$00 ;
 $B3C6 RET             ;
*$B3C7 DEC A           ;
 $B3C8 JR NZ,$B3EC     ;
 $B3CA INC (IY+$05)    ;
 $B3CD LD A,(IY+$04)   ;
 $B3D0 SUB $04         ; {lift X -= 4
 $B3D2 LD (IY+$04),A   ; }
 $B3D5 LD A,(IY+$05)   ;
 $B3D8 CP $52          ; {reached Y=$52?
 $B3DA RET NZ          ; }
 $B3DB INC (HL)        ;
 $B3DC INC (IY+$02)    ;
 $B3DF LD (IY+$04),$DC ;
 $B3E3 LD (IY+$05),$08 ;
 $B3E7 LD (IY+$06),$8F ;
 $B3EB RET             ;
*$B3EC INC (IY+$05)    ;
 $B3EF LD A,(IY+$05)   ;
 $B3F2 CP $48          ; {reached Y=$48?
 $B3F4 RET NZ          ; }
 $B3F5 LD A,$01        ; {set flag $5C00 (lift done)
 $B3F7 LD ($5C00),A    ; }
 $B3FA LD (IY+$06),$7F ;
 $B3FE LD A,$0F        ;
 $B400 LD ($5B98),A    ;
 $B403 CALL $9E5D      ; Populate the $5BD6 object-slot table
 $B406 JP $AE84        ; => Set hero status ($5C06), clear hazard timer ($5C07)

; Staged animation: init object ($5B14), branch on player side
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Room hazard that bounces an object vertically between floor and ceiling,
; starting on whichever side of the screen the hero stands on. Stage 0 picks
; that side and places the object; stage 1 hands off to the ceiling-bound or
; floor-bound mover depending on the object's type, each stepping 1px per frame
; and bouncing off both the opposite bound and the side walls; stage 2 resets
; the state.
c$B409 LD IY,$5B14     ;
 $B40D LD HL,$5C41     ;
 $B410 LD A,(HL)       ;
 $B411 OR A            ; {stage 0?
 $B412 JR NZ,$B436     ; }
 $B414 INC (HL)        ;
 $B415 LD A,(IX+$00)   ;
 $B418 LD C,$01        ;
 $B41A CP $C8          ; player left of $C8?
 $B41C LD (IY+$00),$D8 ; start at bottom (Y=$D8), else top (Y=$08)
 $B420 JR C,$B427      ;
 $B422 DEC C           ;
 $B423 LD (IY+$00),$08 ;
*$B427 LD A,C          ;
 $B428 LD ($5C40),A    ; store side flag ($5C40)
 $B42B LD A,$30        ;
 $B42D LD ($5B15),A    ;
 $B430 LD A,$9E        ;
 $B432 LD ($5B16),A    ;
 $B435 RET             ;
*$B436 CP $01          ; {stage 1 dispatch

; Boss/miniboss state machine: proximity check, phase transitions
; ($5C3C-$5C3E), animation
;
; .
;
; .
;
; A fixed encounter tied to one room: once the hero gets close enough, it plays
; through a sequence of phases and eventually warps the hero to room $28 with a
; fanfare, rather than acting like a roaming creature. Between phases it also

; hero reaches either edge.

                       ; current room

                       ; #R$AE85

 $B630 JR Z,$B676      ; }

 $B661 LD L,A          ; }

 $B669 LD ($5C3C),A    ; }

 $B681 JR Z,$B689      ; }

*$B689 LD A,(IY+$00)   ;

 $B695 LD C,A          ; }

; Fill-pattern variant B (B=$0B, base $F954): init position, draw pattern via
; #R$9A4D
;

;
; .
;
; Stashes the object's position into the $5B14 slot fields, then paints a short

; Resolve conflicting L/R, U/D input via #R$B894 (cancel to 0)
;
; Used by the routines at #R$A34B, #R$A3E1 and #R$AF81.
;
; .
;
; Reads the current input and cancels out impossible presses (both left and
; right, or both up and down at once) before the movement code sees it.
c$B87D CALL $B894    ; Read joystick/keyboard, normalize to Kempston-style
                     ; bitmask
 $B880 LD E,A        ; keep a copy in E
 $B881 AND $03       ; {left and right both pressed?
 $B883 CP $03        ; }
 $B885 JR NZ,$B889   ;
 $B887 XOR A         ; {yes: cancel to 0
 $B888 RET           ; }
*$B889 LD A,E        ; {up and down both pressed?
 $B88A AND $0C       ; }
 $B88C CP $0C        ;
 $B88E JR NZ,$B892   ;
 $B890 XOR A         ; {yes: cancel to 0
 $B891 RET           ; }
*$B892 LD A,E        ; {return E (no conflict)
 $B893 RET           ; }

; Read joystick/keyboard, normalize to Kempston-style bitmask
;
; Used by the routine at #R$B87D.
;
; .
;
; Device selected by ($94AF): 0=keyboard (redefined keys, table at $B8D4),
; 1=Kempston (port $1F), 2=Sinclair 2 (keys 6-0, port $EFFE). Result stored at
; $B87C: bit0=right, bit1=left, bit2=down, bit3=up, bit4=fire.
c$B894 LD HL,$B87C   ;
 $B897 LD (HL),$00   ;
 $B899 LD A,($94AF)  ; {A = device ($94AF)
 $B89C OR A          ; }
 $B89D JP Z,$B8FE    ; zero? keyboard
 $B8A0 DEC A         ; {device=1: Kempston
 $B8A1 JR Z,$B8CC    ; }
 $B8A3 LD BC,$EFFE   ; {device=2: Sinclair, read port $EFFE
 $B8A6 IN A,(C)      ; }
 $B8A8 AND $1F       ;
 $B8AA BIT 0,A       ;
 $B8AC JR NZ,$B8B0   ;
 $B8AE SET 4,(HL)    ;
*$B8B0 BIT 4,A       ;
 $B8B2 JR NZ,$B8B6   ;
 $B8B4 SET 1,(HL)    ;
*$B8B6 BIT 3,A       ;
 $B8B8 JR NZ,$B8BC   ;
 $B8BA SET 0,(HL)    ;
*$B8BC BIT 1,A       ;
 $B8BE JR NZ,$B8C2   ;
 $B8C0 SET 3,(HL)    ;
*$B8C2 BIT 2,A       ;
 $B8C4 JP NZ,$B930   ; => Return normalized input bitmask
 $B8C7 SET 2,(HL)    ;
 $B8C9 JP $B930      ; => Return normalized input bitmask
*$B8CC IN A,($1F)    ; {read the Kempston port $1F
 $B8CE AND $1F       ; }
 $B8D0 LD (HL),A     ; store the result
 $B8D1 JP $B930      ; => Return normalized input bitmask

; Spawn a creature/hazard into slot $5C0E/$5C13 from a room-data entry (HL)
;
; Used by the routine at #R$B93F.
;
;   HL room-data entry ($B99D format)
;   C running spawn counter (persisted across #R$B93F's scan, incremented here)
; O:IX chosen slot ($5C0E or $5C13)
;
; Spawns one creature/hazard from a $B99D table entry. A running spawn counter
; (C, carried over from #R$B93F's scan) picks which of the two dynamic slots it
; goes into and skips the entry entirely once both slots are already filled;
; the entry's own data then supplies the type and X/Y position.
c$B95F BIT 1,C       ; {skip if both slots already filled (bit1 of counter)
 $B961 RET NZ        ; }
 $B962 LD IX,$5C0E   ;
 $B966 BIT 0,C       ; {counter bit0 picks slot ($5C0E/$5C13)
 $B968 JR Z,$B96E    ; }
 $B96A LD IX,$5C13   ;
*$B96E INC C         ; counter++ (mark this slot used)
 $B96F PUSH HL       ;
 $B970 PUSH AF       ;
 $B971 PUSH BC       ;
 $B972 LD (IX+$03),L ; {store own address (IX+3/4)
 $B975 LD (IX+$04),H ; }
 $B978 INC HL        ; {HL -> type byte
 $B979 LD A,(HL)     ; }
 $B97A INC HL        ; {step to the position byte
 $B97B LD C,(HL)     ; }
 $B97C PUSH AF       ;
 $B97D AND $1F       ; {type = entry byte1 AND $1F
 $B97F LD (IX+$02),A ; }
 $B982 POP AF        ;
 $B983 AND $E0       ; {X = entry byte2 high bits
 $B985 LD L,A        ; }
 $B986 LD A,C        ;
 $B987 AND $03       ;
 $B989 RRA           ; {rotate X bits into place
 $B98A RR L          ; }
 $B98C RRA           ;
 $B98D RR L          ;
 $B98F LD (IX+$00),L ;
 $B992 LD A,C        ; {Y from entry byte2
 $B993 AND $FC       ; }
 $B995 ADD A,A       ;
 $B996 LD (IX+$01),A ;
 $B999 POP BC        ;
 $B99A POP AF        ;
 $B99B POP HL        ;
 $B99C RET           ;

; Room-tagged creature/encounter table

; .

;
; Room-tagged creature/encounter table, separate from the per-room $C152 table
; (see Actors.md). 31 entries, 3 bytes each: byte0=room number this entry

; rescans the $B99D table for the room, and awards score via #R$BCF2. In every

; Item pickup/hint check for both creature slots ($5C0E, $5C13)
;
; Used by the routine at #R$B9FA.
;
; .
;
; Per-frame pickup check for the two creature slots ($5C0E, $5C13): if the slot
; holds a collectible item rather than a hazard, and the hero is close enough,
; and the 27-slot inventory log at $5B7C has a free entry, the item is
; collected. A few item types have extra conditions (one latches the current
; room as a bookmark, others only allow pickup mid-animation of another event);
; a successful pickup snaps the hero to the item, starts the pickup animation
; (status 5) and deactivates the item. See Items-Format.md for the log format.

 $BC18 DEC A           ; else index 2
*$BC19 LD ($5C23),A    ;
 $BC1C JP $9EBD        ; => Init $5BD6 object slots from $5C23

; Cycle inventory selection via keys (port $F7FE), animate scroll ($5C21/$5C22)
;
; Used by the routine at #R$B9FA.
;
; .
;
; Handles the player cycling through carried items with the number keys,
; driving the little scroll animation as the selection changes and updating
; which item is actually held.
c$BC1F JR NZ,$BC4A   ; no key pressed? skip to scroll dispatch
 $BC21 LD BC,$F7FE   ;
 $BC24 IN A,(C)      ;
 $BC26 AND $03       ; {keys 1/2 both pressed? RET
 $BC28 CP $03        ; }
 $BC2A RET Z         ;
 $BC2B AND $01       ; {key 1 pressed?
 $BC2D JR NZ,$BC43   ; }
 $BC2F LD A,$01      ; {arm scroll: dir=1, speed=4
 $BC31 LD ($5C21),A  ; }
 $BC34 LD A,$04      ;
 $BC36 LD ($5C22),A  ;
 $BC39 LD HL,$5C23   ;
 $BC3C DEC (HL)      ; selection index--
 $BC3D BIT 7,(HL)    ; {wrapped below 0? snap to $1A
 $BC3F RET Z         ; }
 $BC40 LD (HL),$1A   ;
 $BC42 RET           ;
*$BC43 XOR A         ; {key 2: clear scroll state
 $BC44 LD ($5C21),A  ; }
 $BC47 LD ($5C22),A  ;
*$BC4A LD A,($5C21)  ; {scrolling? skip re-init
 $BC4D OR A          ; }
 $BC4E JR NZ,$BC6C   ;
 $BC50 CALL $9EBD    ; Init $5BD6 object slots from $5C23
 $BC53 LD HL,$5C22   ;
 $BC56 INC (HL)      ;
 $BC57 LD A,(HL)     ; {scroll-speed counter==4?
 $BC58 CP $04        ; }
 $BC5A RET NZ        ;
 $BC5B LD (HL),$00   ;
 $BC5D LD HL,$5C23   ;
 $BC60 INC (HL)      ;
 $BC61 LD A,(HL)     ; {selection index reached $1B (wrap)?
 $BC62 CP $1B        ; }
 $BC64 JP NZ,$9EBD   ; => Init $5BD6 object slots from $5C23
 $BC67 LD (HL),$00   ;
 $BC69 JP $9EBD      ; => Init $5BD6 object slots from $5C23
*$BC6C LD HL,$5C22   ;
 $BC6F DEC (HL)      ;
 $BC70 JP $9EBD      ; => Init $5BD6 object slots from $5C23

; Room $5B98=$0C seesaw trigger: position gate, toggle Y $46/$48, room-state
; trigger
;
; Used by the routine at #R$B9FA.
;
; IX=$5B04 (hero, implicit - always the same object)
;
; A rocking-platform puzzle piece: once the hero stands at the right spot in
; the right room, it rocks them between two Y positions for a few frames, then
; plays an escalating sound cue and resolves.
c$BC73 LD HL,$5C24     ;
 $BC76 LD A,(HL)       ; {flag==$0D? skip
 $BC77 CP $0D          ; }
 $BC79 RET Z           ;
 $BC7A LD A,($5B98)    ; {room==$0C?
 $BC7D CP $0C          ; }
 $BC7F RET NZ          ;
 $BC80 LD A,(IX+$01)   ;
 $BC83 CP $48          ; {Y==$48?
 $BC85 JR Z,$BC8A      ; }
 $BC87 CP $46          ;
 $BC89 RET NZ          ;
*$BC8A LD E,A          ;
 $BC8B LD A,(IX+$00)   ;
 $BC8E CP $34          ; {X<$34? else RET
 $BC90 RET NC          ; }
 $BC91 CP $28          ;
 $BC93 RET C           ;
 $BC94 SET 7,(IX+$03)  ;
 $BC98 LD A,($5C02)    ;
 $BC9B AND $01         ; {frame bit0: toggle Y=$46/$48
 $BC9D JR NZ,$BCAC     ; }
 $BC9F LD (IX+$01),$46 ;
 $BCA3 LD A,E          ;
 $BCA4 CP $48          ;
 $BCA6 JR Z,$BCAC      ;
 $BCA8 LD (IX+$01),$48 ;
*$BCAC LD A,($5C02)    ;
 $BCAF AND $03         ; {frame&3!=0? RET
 $BCB1 RET NZ          ; }
 $BCB2 LD A,$06        ;
 $BCB4 LD ($5C06),A    ; store room-state=6
 $BCB7 LD A,(HL)       ;
 $BCB8 INC (HL)        ;
 $BCB9 CP $0C          ; counter==$0C?
 $BCBB JP Z,$AE84      ; => Set hero status ($5C06), clear hazard timer ($5C07)
 $BCBE SUB $06         ; counter-6
 $BCC0 RET C           ;
 $BCC1 LD C,A          ;
 $BCC2 LD A,$06        ;
 $BCC4 SUB C           ;
 $BCC5 LD L,A          ;
 $BCC6 LD H,$00        ;
 $BCC8 ADD HL,HL       ;
 $BCC9 ADD HL,HL       ;
 $BCCA ADD HL,HL       ;
 $BCCB ADD HL,HL       ;
 $BCCC ADD HL,HL       ;
 $BCCD LD DE,$F928     ; DE=$F928 (sound-effect table)
 $BCD0 ADD HL,DE       ;
 $BCD1 PUSH HL         ;
 $BCD2 LD A,$98        ;
 $BCD4 CALL $9A52      ; Write A to (HL)+$6000 (secondary buffer), then #R$9A62
                       ; dual-write loop
 $BCD7 POP HL          ; {restore HL, advance
 $BCD8 INC HL          ; }
 $BCD9 LD A,$99        ; A=$99 (second byte)
 $BCDB JP $9A52        ; => Write A to (HL)+$6000 (secondary buffer), then
                       ; #R$9A62 dual-write loop

; Negate 4-byte value ($5C18) via CPL chain, falls into #R$BD15 (add DE:BC=1)
;
; Used by the routine at #R$BD75.
;
; .
;
; Negates the 32-bit score value in place, so the shared add routine can be
; reused to subtract.
c$BCDE LD A,(HL)     ; negate 3 bytes (CPL each, unrolled, HL-- between)
 $BCDF CPL           ;
 $BCE0 LD (HL),A     ;
 $BCE1 DEC HL        ;
 $BCE2 LD A,(HL)     ;
 $BCE3 CPL           ;
 $BCE4 LD (HL),A     ;
 $BCE5 DEC HL        ;
 $BCE6 LD A,(HL)     ;
 $BCE7 CPL           ;
 $BCE8 LD (HL),A     ;
 $BCE9 DEC HL        ;
 $BCEA LD A,(HL)     ; {negate the last byte
 $BCEB CPL           ; }
 $BCEC LD (HL),A     ;
 $BCED LD DE,$0001   ; DE=1 (so the add becomes a two-s complement)
 $BCF0 JR $BD15      ;

; Save all registers (context-save wrapper)
;
; Used by the routines at #R$8F47, #R$A851, #R$B4E2, #R$B5DD, #R$B9FA and
; #R$BB5D.
;
; DE score delta to add (passed through to #R$BD11)
;
; Awards a score/timer delta and redraws its display, preserving every register
; around the call so it can be dropped into any piece of game logic without
; disturbing what that code was doing.
c$BCF2 PUSH IX       ; push the main registers (IX,IY,HL,BC,AF)
 $BCF4 PUSH IY       ;
 $BCF6 PUSH HL       ;
 $BCF7 PUSH BC       ;
 $BCF8 PUSH AF       ;
 $BCF9 EXX           ;
 $BCFA PUSH HL       ; push the alternate registers (HL,BC,DE)
 $BCFB PUSH BC       ;
 $BCFC PUSH DE       ;
 $BCFD EXX           ;
 $BCFE CALL $BD11    ; {Add 32-bit value ($5C18) by DE:BC
 $BD01 CALL $BD75    ; }
 $BD04 EXX           ;
 $BD05 POP HL        ; pop the alternate registers
 $BD06 POP BC        ;
 $BD07 POP DE        ;
 $BD08 EXX           ;
 $BD09 POP AF        ; pop the main registers
 $BD0A POP BC        ;
 $BD0B POP HL        ;
 $BD0C POP IY        ;
 $BD0E POP IX        ;
 $BD10 RET           ;

; Add 32-bit value ($5C18) by DE:BC (BC sign-extended from D)
;
; Used by the routine at #R$BCF2.
;
; .
;
; Adds a signed 16-bit amount to the 32-bit score, sign-extending so the same
; routine handles both awards and deductions.
c$BD11 LD IX,$5C18   ; IX=$5C18 (target)
; This entry point is used by the routine at #R$BCDE.
*$BD15 LD BC,$FFFF   ; assume a negative amount (BC=-1)
 $BD18 BIT 7,D       ; {D positive? use 0 instead
 $BD1A JR NZ,$BD1F   ; }
 $BD1C LD BC,$0000   ;
*$BD1F LD L,(IX+$00) ; {HL=(IX+0/1) low word
 $BD22 LD H,(IX+$01) ; }
 $BD25 ADD HL,DE     ; add the low word
 $BD26 LD (IX+$00),L ; {store it back
 $BD29 LD (IX+$01),H ; }
 $BD2C LD L,(IX+$02) ; {HL=(IX+2/3) high word
 $BD2F LD H,(IX+$03) ; }
 $BD32 ADC HL,BC     ; add the high word with carry
 $BD34 LD (IX+$02),L ; {store it back
 $BD37 LD (IX+$03),H ; }
 $BD3A RET           ;

; Print hi-score ($5B78) at screen $5049 via #R$BD78
;
; Used by the routine at #R$BD50.
c$BD3B LD HL,($BD89) ; {save the printer's current source pointer ($BD89)
 $BD3E PUSH HL       ; }
 $BD3F LD HL,$5B78   ; {repoint it at the hi-score ($5B78)
 $BD42 LD ($BD89),HL ; }
 $BD45 LD HL,$5049   ; HL=screen position $5049
 $BD48 CALL $BD78    ; Print current score at screen $5029, falls into #R$BD78
 $BD4B POP HL        ; {restore the original source pointer
 $BD4C LD ($BD89),HL ; }
 $BD4F RET           ;

; New high-score check: compare $5C1B vs stored $5B7B, save if beaten
;
; Used by the routine at #R$8F47.
;
; .
;
; Compares the score just made against the stored high score digit by digit
; and, if it is bigger, copies it over and redraws the display.
c$BD50 LD HL,$5C1B   ; HL = candidate score ($5C1B)
 $BD53 BIT 7,(HL)    ; {already flagged? skip
 $BD55 RET NZ        ; }
 $BD56 LD DE,$5B7B   ; DE = stored high score ($5B7B)
 $BD59 LD B,$04      ; B=4 digits
*$BD5B LD A,(DE)     ; {compare one digit
 $BD5C CP (HL)       ; }
 $BD5D JR C,$BD67    ; candidate bigger? take it
 $BD5F JR Z,$BD62    ; {equal? try the next digit
 $BD61 RET           ; }
*$BD62 DEC HL        ; {step both pointers back
 $BD63 DEC DE        ; }
 $BD64 DJNZ $BD5B    ; loop 4 digits
 $BD66 RET           ;
*$BD67 LD HL,$5C18   ; {HL=$5C18, DE=$5B78
 $BD6A LD DE,$5B78   ; }
 $BD6D LD BC,$0004   ;
 $BD70 LDIR          ; copy the 4-byte score
 $BD72 JP $BD3B      ; Print hi-score ($5B78) at screen $5049 via #R$BD78

; Print current score at screen $5029, falls into #R$BD78
;
; Used by the routine at #R$BCF2.
;
; .
;
; Draws the current score as digits on screen, blanking leading zeros - the
; shared digit-printer also reused by the high-score display.
c$BD75 LD HL,$5029   ; HL=$5029 (screen position)
; This entry point is used by the routine at #R$BD3B.
*$BD78 PUSH HL       ;
 $BD79 LD B,$04      ; B=4 digit cells
*$BD7B LD A,$20      ; A=$20 (space)
 $BD7D CALL $90C6    ; Draw character bitmap
 $BD80 DJNZ $BD7B    ; loop 4 spaces
 $BD82 POP HL        ;
 $BD83 EXX           ;
 $BD84 XOR A         ; {clear leading-zero flag ($5C20)
 $BD85 LD ($5C20),A  ; }
 $BD88 LD HL,$5C18   ; HL=$5C18 (score)
 $BD8B LD DE,$5C1C   ; {DE=$5C1C, BC=4
 $BD8E LD BC,$0004   ; }
 $BD91 LDIR          ; copy score to work buffer
 $BD93 EX DE,HL      ;
 $BD94 DEC HL        ;
 $BD95 LD IX,$5C1C   ; IX=$5C1C (work buffer)
 $BD99 BIT 7,(HL)    ; {sign bit set?
 $BD9B JR Z,$BDA2    ; }
 $BD9D CALL $BCDE    ; Negate 4-byte value ($5C18) via CPL chain, falls into
                     ; #R$BD15
 $BDA0 JR $BDA2      ;
*$BDA2 LD IY,$BE18   ; IY=$BE18 (place-value table)
 $BDA6 LD B,$04      ; B=4 digits
*$BDA8 PUSH BC       ;
 $BDA9 LD C,$00      ; C=0 (digit counter)
 $BDAB LD E,(IY+$00) ; {DE = place value from table
 $BDAE LD D,(IY+$01) ; }
 $BDB1 LD B,(IY+$02) ; B = its high byte
 $BDB4 INC IY        ; IY += 3 (next entry)
 $BDB6 INC IY        ;
 $BDB8 INC IY        ;
 $BDBA CALL $BDDF    ; Repeated-subtraction division
 $BDBD LD A,($5C20)  ; {leading-zero flag set?
 $BDC0 OR A          ; }
 $BDC1 LD A,C        ; {A=digit, non-zero? print it
 $BDC2 JR NZ,$BDCA   ; }
 $BDC4 OR A          ; {digit zero and still leading? skip
 $BDC5 JR Z,$BDD5    ; }
 $BDC7 LD ($5C20),A  ; else clear the flag
*$BDCA ADD A,$30     ; convert digit to ASCII
 $BDCC EXX           ; EXX
 $BDCD CALL $90C6    ; Draw character bitmap
 $BDD0 EXX           ;
 $BDD1 POP BC        ; restore BC
*$BDD2 DJNZ $BDA8    ; loop 4 digits
 $BDD4 RET           ;
*$BDD5 POP BC        ;
 $BDD6 LD A,B        ; {last digit (B==1)?
 $BDD7 CP $01        ; }
 $BDD9 JR NZ,$BDD2   ; no: skip
 $BDDB DEC A         ;
 $BDDC PUSH BC       ;
 $BDDD JR $BDCA      ; force printing a single zero

; Repeated-subtraction division: subtract DE from 32-bit (IX+0..3), C=count
;
; Used by the routine at #R$BD75.
;
;   IX 32-bit value to divide
;   DE low word of the divisor
;   B high byte of the divisor
; O:C quotient (number of successful subtractions)
;
; Divides a 32-bit value by repeatedly subtracting a divisor and counting how
; many times it fit - used by the score/digit-printing code to peel off one
; decimal digit at a time.
c$BDDF LD L,(IX+$00) ; {HL = low word of the value
 $BDE2 LD H,(IX+$01) ; }
 $BDE5 PUSH HL       ; save it
 $BDE6 AND A         ; {low word -= DE
 $BDE7 SBC HL,DE     ; }
 $BDE9 LD (IX+$00),L ; {store it back
 $BDEC LD (IX+$01),H ; }
 $BDEF LD A,(IX+$02) ; {A = byte 2
 $BDF2 PUSH AF       ; }
 $BDF3 SBC A,B       ; {subtract divisor high byte with borrow
 $BDF4 LD (IX+$02),A ; }
 $BDF7 LD A,(IX+$03) ; {A = byte 3
 $BDFA PUSH AF       ; }
 $BDFB SBC A,$00     ; {propagate the borrow
 $BDFD LD (IX+$03),A ; }
 $BE00 JR C,$BE08    ; went negative?
 $BE02 POP AF        ; discard the saved copies
 $BE03 POP AF        ;
 $BE04 POP HL        ;
 $BE05 INC C         ; {count one more subtraction
 $BE06 JR $BDDF      ; }
*$BE08 POP AF        ; {restore byte 3
 $BE09 LD (IX+$03),A ; }
 $BE0C POP AF        ; {restore byte 2
 $BE0D LD (IX+$02),A ; }
 $BE10 POP HL        ; restore the low word
 $BE11 LD (IX+$01),H ; {store it back
 $BE14 LD (IX+$00),L ; }
 $BE17 RET           ;

; Decimal place-value table (1000/100/10/1) for the score printer
b$BE18 DEFB $E8,$03,$00,$64,$00,$00,$0A,$00
 $BE20 DEFB $00,$01,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00
 $BE28 DEFB $00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00
 $BE30 DEFB $00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00
 $BE38 DEFB $00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00
 $BE40 DEFB $00,$00

; Decode room's creatures/hazards from the room data table ($C152)
;
; Used by the routine at #R$9855.
;
; A room number
;
; Decodes the current room's 12-byte record in the $C152 table into the 29-byte
; scratch buffer at $BE24, unpacking it as 3 creature/hazard sub-records of 4
; bytes each (packed type ID, flag bits and raw fields - see Actors.md). An
; all-zero sub-record means an empty slot. Returns A unchanged.
c$BE42 PUSH AF       ; save A (room number)
 $BE43 LD HL,$BE24   ;
 $BE46 LD DE,$BE25   ;
 $BE49 LD BC,$001D   ;
 $BE4C LD (HL),$00   ; {clear 29-byte scratch buffer
 $BE4E LDIR          ; }
 $BE50 LD L,A        ; {HL = room number
 $BE51 LD H,$00      ; }
 $BE53 ADD HL,HL     ;
 $BE54 ADD HL,HL     ;
 $BE55 PUSH HL       ;
 $BE56 ADD HL,HL     ;
 $BE57 POP DE        ;
 $BE58 ADD HL,DE     ;
 $BE59 LD DE,$C152   ; {HL = room data table + A*12
 $BE5C ADD HL,DE     ; }
 $BE5D LD DE,$BE24   ;
 $BE60 LD B,$03      ; B=3 slots
*$BE62 PUSH DE       ;
 $BE63 LD A,(HL)     ;
 $BE64 PUSH AF       ;
 $BE65 AND $0F       ; byte0 low nibble = creature type ID
 $BE67 LD (DE),A     ; {type written twice
 $BE68 INC DE        ; }
 $BE69 LD (DE),A     ;
 $BE6A INC DE        ;
 $BE6B POP AF        ;
 $BE6C AND $80       ; byte0 bit7 = flag
 $BE6E LD (DE),A     ;
 $BE6F INC DE        ;
 $BE70 LD A,(HL)     ;
 $BE71 RRCA          ; byte0 >>= 4 (four RRCA)
 $BE72 RRCA          ;
 $BE73 RRCA          ;
 $BE74 RRCA          ;
 $BE75 AND $07       ; byte0 bits4-6
 $BE77 LD (DE),A     ;
 $BE78 INC DE        ;
 $BE79 INC HL        ;
 $BE7A LD A,(HL)     ;
 $BE7B LD (DE),A     ;
 $BE7C INC DE        ;
 $BE7D INC HL        ;
 $BE7E LD A,(HL)     ;
 $BE7F LD (DE),A     ;
 $BE80 INC DE        ;
 $BE81 INC HL        ;
 $BE82 LD A,(HL)     ;
 $BE83 AND $7F       ; byte3 low 7 bits
 $BE85 LD (DE),A     ;
 $BE86 INC DE        ;
 $BE87 LD A,(HL)     ;
 $BE88 AND $80       ; byte3 bit7
 $BE8A LD (DE),A     ;
 $BE8B INC HL        ;
 $BE8C POP DE        ;
 $BE8D PUSH HL       ;
 $BE8E LD HL,$000A   ; {advance output pointer +10, next slot
 $BE91 ADD HL,DE     ; }
 $BE92 EX DE,HL      ;
 $BE93 POP HL        ;
 $BE94 DJNZ $BE62    ;
 $BE96 POP AF        ; {restore A
 $BE97 RET           ; }

; Dispatch per-creature-type init (jump table $BECA) for the 3 hazard slots
;
; Used by the routine at #R$8F47.
;
; .
;
; Spawns the room's creatures/hazards: for each of the 3 slots decoded from the
; room data table, jumps to the matching type's own setup routine.
c$BE98 LD B,$03      ; B=3 slots
 $BE9A LD DE,$BE24   ; DE = decoded record ($BE24)
 $BE9D PUSH IX       ;
 $BE9F LD IX,$5B08   ; IX = first object slot ($5B08)
*$BEA3 PUSH BC       ;
 $BEA4 PUSH DE       ;
 $BEA5 LD A,(DE)     ; A = creature type
 $BEA6 LD L,A        ; {zero-extend into HL
 $BEA7 LD H,$00      ; }
 $BEA9 ADD HL,HL     ; type *= 2
 $BEAA LD BC,$BECA   ; {HL = jump table entry ($BECA + type*2)
 $BEAD ADD HL,BC     ; }
 $BEAE LD A,(HL)     ; {A = handler low byte
 $BEAF INC HL        ; }
 $BEB0 LD H,(HL)     ; {HL = handler address
 $BEB1 LD L,A        ; }
 $BEB2 PUSH DE       ; {IY = record pointer
 $BEB3 POP IY        ; }
 $BEB5 CALL $BEC9    ; Jump to handler in HL (dispatch tail of #R$BE98)
 $BEB8 LD DE,$0004   ; {IX += 4 (next object slot)
 $BEBB ADD IX,DE     ; }
 $BEBD POP DE        ;
 $BEBE LD HL,$000A   ; {DE += 10 (next record)
 $BEC1 ADD HL,DE     ; }
 $BEC2 EX DE,HL      ;
 $BEC3 POP BC        ; {loop 3 slots
 $BEC4 DJNZ $BEA3    ; }
 $BEC6 POP IX        ;
 $BEC8 RET           ;

; Jump to handler in HL (dispatch tail of #R$BE98)
;
; Used by the routine at #R$BE98.
c$BEC9 JP (HL)       ;

; Creature-type handler jump table (used by #R$BE98)
b$BECA DEFB $DC,$BE,$DD,$BE,$22,$BF,$67,$BF
 $BED2 DEFB $BB,$BF,$F6,$BF,$54,$C0,$69,$C0
 $BEDA DEFB $35,$C1

; No-op stub (RET)
c$BEDC RET           ;

; Move object along X by 2px, bounce off walls/edges
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Slides an object sideways a couple of pixels each frame and turns it round
; when it meets a wall or the edge of the room - the horizontal half of the
; simple creature movement pair.
c$BEDD BIT 0,(IY+$08) ; template already applied?
 $BEE1 JR NZ,$BEE6    ;
 $BEE3 CALL $C135     ; no: stamp it via #R$C135
*$BEE6 BIT 7,(IY+$07) ; direction flag set?
 $BEEA LD A,(IX+$00)  ; A = X position
 $BEED JR NZ,$BF02    ;
 $BEEF SUB $02        ; {move -2, check underflow
 $BEF1 JR C,$BF08     ; }
 $BEF3 LD (IX+$00),A  ; store the new X
 $BEF6 CALL $C0FD     ; Wrapper: scan tile below feet via #R$A2AC, flag at
                      ; $C12D
 $BEF9 LD A,($C12D)   ; {blocked ($C12D)?
 $BEFC OR A           ; }
 $BEFD JR NZ,$BF08    ;
 $BEFF JP $C0AC       ; => Advance animation frame
*$BF02 ADD A,$02      ;
 $BF04 CP $E7         ;
 $BF06 JR C,$BF13     ;
*$BF08 LD A,(IY+$07)  ; A = direction flag
 $BF0B XOR $80        ; {flip it
 $BF0D LD (IY+$07),A  ; }
 $BF10 JP $C0AC       ; => Advance animation frame
*$BF13 LD (IX+$00),A  ;
 $BF16 CALL $C109     ; Wrapper
 $BF19 LD A,($C12E)   ;
 $BF1C OR A           ;
 $BF1D JR NZ,$BF08    ;
 $BF1F JP $C0AC       ; => Advance animation frame

; Move object -X by 2px (timed via #R$BFA0), bounce via #R$C0FD
;
; .
;

;
; Moves an object left on a timer, reversing when it runs into something - the
; mirror of #R$BFBB.

*$BF9A INC (IY+$00)    ;
 $BF9D JP $C0AC        ; => Advance animation frame

; Countdown timer (IY+8): init via #R$9390 if zero, else decrement
;
; Used by the routines at #R$BF67, #R$BFBB, #R$BFF6 and #R$C069.
;
;   C low bit merged into new random timer value
;   IY object (timer at +8)
; O:Zf set when timer reaches 0
;
; A shared per-object countdown, reseeded with a random-ish value each time it
; runs out - used to stagger creature behavior changes so objects don't all act
; in lockstep.
c$BFA0 LD A,(IY+$08) ; A = timer ((IY+8))
 $BFA3 OR A          ; {still running? just decrement
 $BFA4 JR NZ,$BFB2   ; }
 $BFA6 CALL $C135    ; gate/init via #R$C135
 $BFA9 CALL $9390    ; Pseudo-random byte
 $BFAC AND $7F       ; {mask the random value, fold in C
 $BFAE OR C          ; }
 $BFAF LD (IY+$08),A ; {store it, then reload
*$BFB2 LD A,(IY+$08) ; }
 $BFB5 DEC A         ; {count down, zero? RET
 $BFB6 RET Z         ; }
 $BFB7 LD (IY+$08),A ; store the new value
 $BFBA RET           ;

; Move object +X by 2px (timed via #R$BFA0), bounce via #R$C109
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Moves an object right on a timer, reversing when it runs into something - one
; of the four timed single-direction movers the creature code picks between.
c$BFBB LD C,$01        ;
 $BFBD CALL $BFA0      ; Countdown timer
 $BFC0 LD (IX+$02),$7F ;
 $BFC4 RET NZ          ;
 $BFC5 SET 7,(IY+$07)  ;
 $BFC9 LD A,(IX+$00)   ;
 $BFCC ADD A,$02       ;
 $BFCE CP $E7          ;
 $BFD0 JR C,$BFE1      ;
 $BFD2 LD (IX+$02),$7F ;
 $BFD6 XOR A           ;
 $BFD7 LD (IY+$08),A   ;
 $BFDA LD A,(IY+$01)   ;
 $BFDD LD (IY+$00),A   ;
 $BFE0 RET             ;
*$BFE1 LD (IX+$00),A   ;
 $BFE4 CALL $C109      ; Wrapper
 $BFE7 LD A,($C12E)    ;
 $BFEA OR A            ;
 $BFEB JR NZ,$BFF0     ;
 $BFED JP $C0AC        ; => Advance animation frame
*$BFF0 DEC (IY+$00)    ;
 $BFF3 JP $C0AC        ; => Advance animation frame

; Move object down 2px per tick, animating; continues at $C000
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Moves an object down the screen a couple of pixels each time its countdown
; fires, cycling its animation frame as it goes, and plays a sound once it
; reaches the bottom or hits something. Careful with the $C000 entry point:
; that address is only this routine's continuation in the main bank - #R$8F47
; and #R$9491 page in bank $16 first and so reach a completely different $C000
; (the music player), which this disassembly never shows.
c$BFF6 LD C,$01        ;
 $BFF8 CALL $BFA0      ; Countdown timer
 $BFFB LD (IX+$02),$7F ; frame=$7F (idle)
 $BFFF RET NZ          ;
; This entry point is used by the routines at #R$8F47 and #R$9491.
*$C000 LD A,(IX+$01)   ;
 $C003 ADD A,$02       ; Y += 2
 $C005 CP $67          ; {past bottom ($67)?
 $C007 JR C,$C012      ; }
 $C009 LD (IX+$02),$7F ;
 $C00D LD (IY+$08),$00 ; clear timer
 $C011 RET             ;
*$C012 LD (IX+$01),A   ; store new Y
 $C015 CALL $C121      ; Wrapper: scan tile below-right via #R$A30B, flag at
                       ; $C131
 $C018 LD A,($C132)    ; {blocked below? reverse branch
 $C01B OR A            ; }
 $C01C JR NZ,$C03A     ;
 $C01E LD A,(IY+$07)   ;
 $C021 INC A           ;
 $C022 LD (IY+$07),A   ;
 $C025 AND $06         ; {cycle of 4 frames
 $C027 RRCA            ; }
 $C028 CP $02          ;
 $C02A JR NZ,$C030     ;
 $C02C DEC (IY+$07)    ;
 $C02F DEC A           ;
*$C030 LD C,A          ;
 $C031 ADD A,(IY+$04)  ; frame = base + cycle
 $C034 LD (IX+$02),A   ;
 $C037 JP $C0DA        ;
*$C03A DEC (IX+$01)    ; blocked: back up 1px
 $C03D INC (IY+$07)    ;
 $C040 LD A,(IY+$07)   ;
 $C043 AND $06         ;
 $C045 RRCA            ;
 $C046 JR NZ,$C030     ;
 $C048 LD (IY+$08),A   ;
 $C04B LD (IX+$02),$7F ;
 $C04F LD A,$05        ; sound effect 5
 $C051 JP $C4B2        ; => Sound-effect dispatcher wrapper

; Idle-frame check ($55/$7F), else #R$C0AC advance animation
c$C054 BIT 0,(IY+$08) ; template already applied? (IY+8) bit0
 $C058 JR NZ,$C05D    ;
 $C05A CALL $C135     ; gate/init via #R$C135
*$C05D LD A,(IX+$02)  ;
 $C060 CP $55         ; {frame $55 (settled)? RET
 $C062 RET Z          ; }
 $C063 CP $7F         ; {frame $7F (idle)? RET
 $C065 RET Z          ; }
 $C066 JP $C0AC       ; => Advance animation frame

; Advance animation frame counter (IY+7), compute sprite frame (IX+2)
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Steps a creature to its next animation frame, cycling back to the start when
; it runs off the end, and turns that into the sprite frame the drawing code
; reads.
c$C069 LD C,$11       ; C=$11 (timer reseed bits)
 $C06B CALL $BFA0     ; Countdown timer
 $C06E RET NZ         ;
 $C06F INC (IY+$07)   ; frame counter++
 $C072 BIT 4,(IY+$07) ; cycle finished (bit4)?
 $C076 JR Z,$C085     ;
 $C078 LD A,(IY+$07)  ; {keep only the direction bit
 $C07B AND $80        ; }
 $C07D LD (IY+$07),A  ; store it back
 $C080 XOR A          ; {clear the timer
 $C081 LD (IY+$08),A  ; }
 $C084 RET            ;
*$C085 LD A,(IY+$07)  ; A = frame counter
 $C088 AND $0E        ; {keep bits 1-3, halve
 $C08A RRCA           ; }
 $C08B BIT 2,A        ; {second half of the cycle?
 $C08D JR Z,$C092     ; }
 $C08F CPL            ; {yes: run it backwards
 $C090 AND $03        ; }
*$C092 LD C,A         ; C = frame index
 $C093 ADD A,(IY+$04) ; {frame = base ((IY+4)) + index
 $C096 LD (IX+$02),A  ; }
 $C099 BIT 7,(IY+$02) ;
 $C09D RET Z          ;
 $C09E LD A,(IY+$03)  ;
 $C0A1 CP $04         ;
 $C0A3 JR NC,$C0DA    ;
 $C0A5 LD A,C         ;
 $C0A6 CP (IY+$03)    ;
 $C0A9 RET NZ         ;
 $C0AA JR $C0DA       ;

; Advance animation frame; check player collision, trigger effect via #R$AE85
;
; Used by the routines at #R$BEDD, #R$BF22, #R$BF67, #R$BFBB and #R$C054.
;
; .
;
; The shared "tick a creature" finisher: advances its animation to the next
; frame and, on the right frame, checks whether the hero is close enough to be
; hit, firing a status trigger if so.
c$C0AC LD A,(IY+$07)  ; {A = frame counter
 $C0AF INC A          ; }
 $C0B0 AND $87        ; {wrap to 7 bits, store
 $C0B2 LD (IY+$07),A  ; }
 $C0B5 AND $7E        ; {index from the counter bits
 $C0B7 RRCA           ; }
 $C0B8 ADD A,(IY+$04) ; {frame = base ((IY+4)) + index
 $C0BB LD (IX+$02),A  ; }
 $C0BE LD A,(IY+$07)  ;
 $C0C1 LD (IX+$03),A  ;
 $C0C4 BIT 7,(IY+$02) ; {skip unless (IY+2) high bit set
 $C0C8 RET Z          ; }
 $C0C9 LD A,(IY+$03)  ; A = (IY+3)
 $C0CC CP $04         ; {4 or more? go straight to the hit check
 $C0CE JR NC,$C0DA    ; }
 $C0D0 LD A,(IY+$07)  ;
 $C0D3 AND $06        ;
 $C0D5 RRCA           ;
 $C0D6 CP (IY+$03)    ;
 $C0D9 RET NZ         ;
; This entry point is used by the routines at #R$BFF6 and #R$C069.
*$C0DA PUSH IY        ; {IY=player
 $C0DC LD IY,$5B04    ; }
 $C0E0 CALL $9140     ; Classify object type ((IX+2)) into a size/category flag
 $C0E3 POP IY         ;
 $C0E5 RET NC         ;
 $C0E6 LD C,$18       ; C=$18 (default trigger)
 $C0E8 LD A,($5C06)   ; {status ($5C06) past $0F? RET
 $C0EB CP $0F         ; }
 $C0ED RET NC         ;
 $C0EE OR A           ; {status non-zero? use the default
 $C0EF JR NZ,$C0F9    ; }
 $C0F1 LD A,($A101)   ; {flag $A101 set? use the default
 $C0F4 OR A           ; }
 $C0F5 JR NZ,$C0F9    ;
 $C0F7 LD C,$1A       ; else trigger $1A
*$C0F9 LD A,C         ; {trigger via #R$AE85
 $C0FA JP $AE85       ; }

; Wrapper: scan tile below feet via #R$A2AC, flag at $C12D
;
; Used by the routines at #R$BEDD and #R$BF67.
c$C0FD PUSH IY       ;
 $C0FF LD IY,$C12D   ;
 $C103 CALL $A2AC    ; Scan tile column below feet against solid-tile list
                     ; ($A24B/$A271), flag
 $C106 POP IY        ;
 $C108 RET           ;

; Wrapper: scan tile right via #R$A2FA, flag at $C12D
;
; Used by the routines at #R$BEDD and #R$BFBB.
c$C109 PUSH IY       ;
 $C10B LD IY,$C12D   ;
 $C10F CALL $A2FA    ; Scan tile column right of object (X+23) via #R$A2B2
 $C112 POP IY        ;
 $C114 RET           ;

; Wrapper: scan tile via #R$A31F, flag at $C131
;
; Used by the routine at #R$BF22.
c$C115 PUSH IY       ;
 $C117 LD IY,$C131   ;
 $C11B CALL $A31F    ; Scan tile at (X+12) against special-tile list
                     ; ($A242/$A268), flag
 $C11E POP IY        ;
 $C120 RET           ;

; Wrapper: scan tile below-right via #R$A30B, flag at $C131
;
; Used by the routines at #R$BF22 and #R$BFF6.
c$C121 PUSH IY       ;
 $C123 LD IY,$C131   ;
 $C127 CALL $A30B    ; Scan tile below-right of feet (X+12,Y+24) via #R$A328
 $C12A POP IY        ;
 $C12C RET           ;

; Tile-scan result flags (used by #R$C0FD/#R$C109)
b$C12D DEFB $00

; Unused/scratch flag bytes (NOP-initialized, $C12E-$C132)
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Mostly padding, but the $C135 entry point here is real: it stamps an object
; with its starting position and frame from a template, and is called whenever
; a creature needs (re)initialising.
c$C12E NOP            ; unused scratch bytes (7 NOPs)
 $C12F NOP            ;
 $C130 NOP            ;
 $C131 NOP            ;
 $C132 NOP            ;
 $C133 NOP            ;
 $C134 NOP            ;
; This entry point is used by the routines at #R$BEDD, #R$BF22, #R$BFA0 and
; #R$C054.
*$C135 SET 0,(IY+$08) ; set gate flag (IY+8)=1
 $C139 LD A,(IY+$05)  ; {copy X from the template
 $C13C LD (IX+$00),A  ; }
 $C13F LD A,(IY+$06)  ; {copy Y
 $C142 LD (IX+$01),A  ; }
 $C145 LD A,(IY+$04)  ; {copy the frame
 $C148 LD (IX+$02),A  ; }
 $C14B LD A,(IY+$07)  ; {copy the direction flag
 $C14E LD (IX+$03),A  ; }
 $C151 RET            ;

; Sound-effect dispatcher wrapper: save regs, call #R$C4BC
;
; Used by the routines at #R$A3E1, #R$A8AB, #R$AA3C, #R$B0B6, #R$BB5D and
; #R$BFF6.
;
; A sound-effect index (0-6)
;
; Plays a sound effect by number without disturbing any registers - the generic
; "make this sound" entry point called from all over the game.
c$C4B2 PUSH HL       ;
 $C4B3 PUSH DE       ;
 $C4B4 PUSH BC       ;
 $C4B5 CALL $C4BC    ; Sound-effect table lookup
 $C4B8 POP BC        ;
 $C4B9 POP DE        ;
 $C4BA POP HL        ;
 $C4BB RET           ;

; Sound-effect table lookup ($C55B): push handler address, E=$10, tail-call
;
; Used by the routine at #R$C4B2.
;
; .
;
; Turns a sound-effect number into the address of its player routine and
; tail-jumps there, so the effect runs as if it had been called directly.
c$C4BC CP $07        ; {index past 6? RET
 $C4BE RET NC        ; }
 $C4BF ADD A,A       ; index *= 2
 $C4C0 LD L,A        ; {HL = index
 $C4C1 LD H,$00      ; }
 $C4C3 LD DE,$C55B   ; {HL = $C55B + index
 $C4C6 ADD HL,DE     ; }
 $C4C7 LD E,(HL)     ; {DE = handler address
 $C4C8 INC HL        ; }
 $C4C9 LD D,(HL)     ;
 $C4CA PUSH DE       ; push it as the return address
 $C4CB LD E,$10      ; E=$10 (speaker bit mask)
 $C4CD RET           ;

; Beeper tone-sweep effect (raw OUT $FE)
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Sweeps the beeper through a falling pitch by halving its delay each pass - a
; short "whoop" cue rather than a fixed tone.
c$C4CE LD H,$7F      ; H=$7F (sweep count)
*$C4D0 XOR A         ;
 $C4D1 LD B,$0A      ; B=$0A (bit count)
*$C4D3 PUSH BC       ;
 $C4D4 LD B,H        ; B = H (duty)
*$C4D5 OUT ($FE),A   ; toggle beeper
 $C4D7 EX (SP),HL    ; {delay
 $C4D8 EX (SP),HL    ; }
 $C4D9 DJNZ $C4D5    ; loop duty
 $C4DB XOR $10       ; flip the speaker bit
 $C4DD POP BC        ;
 $C4DE DJNZ $C4D3    ; loop bits
 $C4E0 SRL H         ; {H >>= 2 (raise the pitch)
 $C4E2 SRL H         ; }
 $C4E4 LD A,H        ; {H reached 0?
 $C4E5 OR A          ; }
 $C4E6 JR NZ,$C4D0   ;
 $C4E8 RET           ;

; Play sound effect (raw OUT $FE beeper timing loop)
;
; .
;
; .
;
; A beeper sound-effect player: plays back a sample, then a tone sweep,
; entirely through timed port writes rather than an interrupt-driven player.
c$C4E9 LD HL,$0000   ; HL=0 (sample pointer)
 $C4EC LD BC,$2328   ; BC=$2328 (sample count)
*$C4EF LD A,$23      ; {delay = $23 - B
 $C4F1 SUB B         ; }
 $C4F2 JR Z,$C4F9    ; zero? no delay
 $C4F4 PUSH BC       ;
 $C4F5 LD B,A        ; B = delay
*$C4F6 DJNZ $C4F6    ; busy-wait
 $C4F8 POP BC        ;
*$C4F9 LD A,(HL)     ; {read sample byte
 $C4FA INC HL        ; }
 $C4FB AND E         ; {mask and send to speaker
 $C4FC OUT ($FE),A   ; }
 $C4FE DEC BC        ; BC -= 4 (four DEC BC)
 $C4FF DEC BC        ;
 $C500 DEC BC        ;
 $C501 DEC BC        ;
 $C502 LD A,C        ; {count exhausted?
 $C503 OR B          ; }
 $C504 JR NZ,$C4EF   ;
 $C506 LD H,$03      ; H=3 (sweep count)
*$C508 XOR A         ;
 $C509 LD B,$0A      ; B=$0A (bit count)
*$C50B PUSH BC       ;
 $C50C LD B,H        ; B = H (duty)
*$C50D OUT ($FE),A   ; toggle speaker
 $C50F EX (SP),HL    ; {delay
 $C510 EX (SP),HL    ; }
 $C511 DJNZ $C50D    ; loop duty
 $C513 XOR $10       ; flip the speaker bit
 $C515 POP BC        ;
 $C516 DJNZ $C50B    ; loop bits
 $C518 SCF           ; {shift a 1 into H
 $C519 RL H          ; }
 $C51B LD A,H        ; {H all ones?
 $C51C CP $FF        ; }
 $C51E JR NZ,$C508   ;
 $C520 RET           ;

; Play noise-type sound effect (R-register based)
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Makes a noise burst by toggling the speaker with bits taken from low ROM
; ($0000-$003F) at an offset driven by the refresh register - a cheap random
; source, so the result is hiss rather than a tone.
c$C521 LD B,$64      ;
*$C523 LD A,R        ; A = R (refresh counter, pseudo-random)
 $C525 AND $3F       ; {index 0-$3F into low ROM
 $C527 LD L,A        ; }
 $C528 LD H,$00      ;
 $C52A LD A,(HL)     ; {read ROM byte, keep only the speaker bit
 $C52B AND $10       ; }
 $C52D OUT ($FE),A   ;
 $C52F DJNZ $C523    ;
 $C531 RET           ;

; Beeper tone effect variant A (HL=$03C8), falls into #R$C53A
c$C532 LD HL,$03C8   ;
 $C535 JR $C53A      ;

; Beeper tone effect variant B (HL=$0564)
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Plays a fixed-pitch beep by toggling the speaker on a timed loop - the
; longer-period twin of #R$C532.
c$C537 LD HL,$0564   ; HL=$0564 (tone period)
; This entry point is used by the routine at #R$C532.
*$C53A XOR A         ; {A=0, B = period
 $C53B LD B,L        ; }
 $C53C OUT ($FE),A   ; speaker low
*$C53E DJNZ $C53E    ; busy-wait
 $C540 LD A,E        ; {speaker high
 $C541 OUT ($FE),A   ; }
 $C543 LD B,L        ; B = period again
*$C544 DJNZ $C544    ; {busy-wait delay
 $C546 DEC H         ; }
 $C547 JR NZ,$C53A   ; loop until H runs out
 $C549 RET           ;

; Data block at C54A
b$C54A DEFB $21

; Beeper noise/sample effect (raw OUT $FE)
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Plays a short noise burst by streaming bytes straight to the speaker port,
; used for impact-type effects.
c$C54B NOP           ; {timing pad (two NOPs)
 $C54C NOP           ; }
 $C54D LD B,L        ; B = outer count
*$C54E LD C,$05      ; C=5 (inner count)
*$C550 LD A,(HL)     ; {read a sample byte, mask it
 $C551 AND E         ; }
 $C552 OUT ($FE),A   ; send it to the speaker
 $C554 INC HL        ; {advance, count down
 $C555 DEC C         ; }
 $C556 JR NZ,$C550   ; loop 5 bytes
 $C558 DJNZ $C54E    ; loop the outer count
 $C55A RET           ;

; Movement-script entry-point table (41 entries, half-byte-offset into $5BAF)
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Read by #R$BB62's object-init tail using a byte read from the fixed-slot
; address (template bytes 7/8, see #R$5B55) as index - not from the template
; directly. The resulting byte is doubled and added to $5BAF to give a byte
; offset into the shared movement-script bytecode pool there, stored at
; IX+$15/$16 as the script start address (the field #R$B94E reads scripts
; from). Values are strictly ascending ($00-$89, i.e. real offsets 0-274) -
; stored halved so a single byte can address the whole pool. Scripts are
; variable-length (no fixed record size), so consecutive entries aren't evenly
; spaced. Since the index comes from a live fixed-slot byte rather than a
; template constant, the chosen script can vary at runtime.
b$5B00 DEFB $00,$02,$04,$09,$10,$17,$1E,$26
 $5B08 DEFB $2A,$31,$38,$3C,$44,$48,$4D,$4F
 $5B10 DEFB $52,$55,$58,$5A,$5F,$62,$65,$67
 $5B18 DEFB $6A,$6D,$72,$75,$7C,$7F,$84,$89
 $5B20 DEFB $8E,$91,$95,$97,$9C,$9D,$9E,$9F
 $5B28 DEFB $A0

; Formation-tag to group-index lookup table (44 entries, indexed by tag & $3F)
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Indexed by #R$BA5F from the spawn-timeline's tag byte (C, masked to bits 0-5,
; though only 44 entries are populated); each entry is a group index used to
; look up the per-group spawn budget in the table at $5CF4. Values are strictly
; ascending ($00-$FB), consistent with a byte-offset/threshold table rather
; than raw group indices.
b$5B29 DEFB $00,$04,$09,$0D,$11,$15,$19,$1E
 $5B31 DEFB $26,$30,$38,$40,$48,$50,$58,$5D
 $5B39 DEFB $61,$66,$6B,$6F,$73,$77,$7E,$85
 $5B41 DEFB $89,$90,$95,$9C,$A4,$A8,$B3,$BA
 $5B49 DEFB $C1,$C5,$CA,$D1,$D8,$DD,$E1,$E5
 $5B51 DEFB $E9,$F0,$F4,$FB

; Spawn-template table (9 bytes/entry, indexed by #R$BA5F as index*9 + $5B55)
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Each 9-byte template initializes a newly-spawned object (field mapping
; confirmed by matching self-modified write targets to their instruction
; operands in #R$BB62's init block): byte 0 -> IX+$05; byte 1 -> IX+$12; byte 2
; -> IX+$1A; byte 3 (+difficulty offset $9C41, clamped) -> IX+$1B; byte 4 ->
; IX+$11; bytes 5/6 (little-endian) -> IX+$02/$03; bytes 7/8 (little-endian) ->
; a fixed-slot address ($9D1E/$9D24/$9D2A, one of #R$B730's 4 persistent object
; slots - $9D30 never observed). IX+$02/$03 is NOT a code pointer despite
; resembling one: every one of the 10 templates' values resolves exactly to
; either a record on the #R$6B42 17-byte descriptor grid ($6B42+17*n -
; $6BCA=record 8, $6B64/$6B75/$6B86/$6BA8=records 2/3/4/6) or an entry in the
; #R$6BDB 6-byte explosion/state-descriptor table ($6BDB+6*n -
; $6BDB/$6BF9/$6BFF/$6C05=entries 0/5/6/7); $6B42's own IY+$02/$03 field is
; itself something #R$7DC9 *writes* (a decoded graphics sub-pointer) rather
; than executable code, and the raw bytes at these addresses don't decode as
; coherent Z80. So IX+$02/$03 is an index/pointer into one of two shared
; descriptor-record tables, read as data by an as-yet-unlocated per-object
; routine, not called as a handler. Bytes 7/8's address is used twice: #R$BB62
; reads one byte from it to select the object's movement script (see #R$5B00),
; and after all objects for this call are spawned, a word at that address is
; read, swapped via EX (SP),HL, and written back - apparently linking the slot
; to the newly-spawned object(s), exact mechanism not fully traced. Byte 1 also
; happens to land on $5B56, the same address written directly as a
; screen/timing poke by #R$A612's config word $0A and timeline command $FB -
; unrelated dual use of that literal address, not a field alias.
b$5B55 DEFB $0B,$06,$00,$20,$00
 $5B5A DEFW $6BDB,$9D24
 $5B5E DEFB $09,$01,$00,$10,$01
 $5B63 DEFW $6B64,$9D1E
 $5B67 DEFB $05,$01,$81,$08,$04
 $5B6C DEFW $6B86,$9D2A
 $5B70 DEFB $0C,$07,$83,$18,$01
 $5B75 DEFW $6BA8,$9D2A
 $5B79 DEFB $0E,$1E,$81,$C0,$02
 $5B7E DEFW $6C05,$9D1E
 $5B82 DEFB $06,$01,$80,$00,$04
 $5B87 DEFW $6B86,$9D2A
 $5B8B DEFB $0A,$01,$00,$14,$01
 $5B90 DEFW $6B75,$9D1E
 $5B94 DEFB $11,$01,$80,$10,$01
 $5B99 DEFW $6BF9,$9D1E
 $5B9D DEFB $11,$01,$80,$10,$01
 $5BA2 DEFW $6BFF,$9D1E
 $5BA6 DEFB $0C,$1A,$81,$48,$01
 $5BAB DEFW $6BA8,$9D2A

; Per-level configuration table (20 bytes/row)
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Read by #R$A612: row = $61D4 + 20*(wave-formation-tag+1).
; .
; One 20-byte per-level row, confirmed field-by-field from #R$A612's 6-word
; SP-trick pop (offsets are byte offsets into the row): $00 word -> $9C57,
; cursor into the colour-scheme table (see #R$A54D, values land in
; $9C59/$9C5A); $02 word -> $9BA5, cursor into this level's timeline table (3
; bytes/entry, see #R$C9AF); $04 word -> $9BFD, this level's scenery-script
; pointer (see #R$A3A0); $06 word -> combined with the current object's IX+$0A

; Init menu screen: wipe, draw player boxes, labels, fill buffer
;
; Used by the routines at #R$A5C0, #R$A6BB, #R$A6E5 and #R$A894.
;
; A colour/type for the wipe transition ($9C59)
;
; Sets the wipe colour, runs the #R$C6A6 wipe effect, draws the player-panel
; box graphics (#R$6AD4, which uses #R$6B09), prints the "PLAYER ONE"/"PLAYER
; TWO" label, draws two box variants via #R$66DE, then fast-fills a buffer at
; $FA79 downward with the word $3D00 (261 words) using a PUSH-based stack
; trick, and finally calls #R$C772.
@label=init_menu_screen
c$6498 LD ($9C59),A  ; set active colour/type for the wipe effect
 $649B CALL $C6A6    ; Screen wipe transition effect
 $649E CALL $6AD4    ; Draw both players' panel borders
 $64A1 LD A,$03      ; "PLAYER ONE"/"PLAYER TWO"
 $64A3 CALL $6648    ; Print message N from table $627A
 $64A6 LD A,$01      ; select box variant 1
 $64A8 CALL $66DE    ; Print a player's score at its HUD position
 $64AB INC A         ; {draw box variant 2
 $64AC CALL $66DE    ; }
 $64AF DI            ; {disable interrupts, save SP, point SP at fill target
 $64B0 LD ($64C8),SP ; $FA79
 $64B4 LD SP,$FA79   ; }
 $64B7 LD HL,$3D00   ; {HL=fill value $3D00, BC=261 (word count)
 $64BA LD BC,$0105   ; }
*$64BD PUSH HL       ; {fill loop: push HL twice per iteration (fast memory
 $64BE PUSH HL       ; fill via stack)
 $64BF DEC BC        ;
 $64C0 LD A,C        ;
 $64C1 OR B          ;
 $64C2 JR NZ,$64BD   ; }
 $64C4 CALL $C772    ; Fast column mover
 $64C7 LD SP,$0000   ; !!MUT-ARG!! reset SP (restored by caller) (patched by
                     ; $64B0)
 $64CA EI            ; {re-enable interrupts, return
 $64CB RET           ; }

; Print character to screen using ROM font (fattened, double-height)
;
; Used by the routines at #R$6626, #R$6663, #R$67F1, #R$6989 and #R$A6E5.
;
; A ASCII character code to print
;
; Draws an ASCII character at the cursor (#R$9CC7) as an emboldened,
; double-height glyph spanning two character cells. Each ROM font row (table at
; $3C00 + code * 8) is smeared one pixel left and right so the glyph prints
; bold, then written to two consecutive screen rows to stretch it vertically,
; and the two bytes at $9CC9 colour both cells. Control codes below $20 are
; dispatched instead through the small jump table at #R$65B3, and the character
; just printed is left in $9CCB.
@label=print_char
c$64CC PUSH AF       ; {Save AF/HL/DE/BC
 $64CD PUSH HL       ;
 $64CE PUSH DE       ;
 $64CF PUSH BC       ; }
 $64D0 LD C,A        ; C=char code
 $64D1 LD A,($9CCB)  ; {Printing is suppressed while the skip flag ($9CCB)
 $64D4 CP $20        ; holds a control code}
 $64D6 JP C,$6594    ; jump to control-code path if printing suppressed
 $64D9 LD A,C        ; {Codes below $20 print nothing
 $64DA CP $20        ; }
 $64DC JP C,$658C    ; jump to blank-glyph exit if char<$20
 $64DF CP $FE        ; Nor does the $FE space-pad code
 $64E1 JP Z,$658C    ; jump to blank-glyph exit if char=$FE
 $64E4 LD HL,($9CC7) ; {load cursor position
 $64E7 LD DE,($9CC9) ; }
 $64EB LD BC,$0020   ; {Colour this cell and the one 32 bytes below it from the
 $64EE LD (HL),E     ; two bytes at $9CC9
 $64EF ADD HL,BC     ;
 $64F0 LD (HL),D     ;
 $64F1 SBC HL,BC     ;
 $64F3 INC HL        ; }
 $64F4 LD ($9CC7),HL ; store advanced cursor column
 $64F7 DEC HL        ; {ROM font address for this character = $3C00 + code * 8
 $64F8 RLCA          ;
 $64F9 RLCA          ;
 $64FA RLCA          ;
 $64FB LD D,A        ;
 $64FC AND $F8       ;
 $64FE LD E,A        ;
 $64FF XOR D         ;
 $6500 ADD A,$3C     ;
 $6502 LD D,A        ; }
 $6503 LD A,H        ; {Convert the attribute address into the matching screen
 $6504 RLCA          ; bitmap address
 $6505 RLCA          ;
 $6506 RLCA          ;
 $6507 XOR $82       ;
 $6509 LD H,A        ;
 $650A EX DE,HL      ; }
 $650B XOR A         ; {Blank the three pixel rows above the glyph
 $650C LD (DE),A     ;
 $650D INC D         ;
 $650E LD (DE),A     ;
 $650F INC D         ;
 $6510 LD (DE),A     ;
 $6511 INC D         ;
 $6512 INC L         ; }
 $6513 LD A,(HL)     ; {Row 0: fatten the glyph byte to (b | b<<1 | b>>1), mask
 $6514 RRCA          ; it and store to two screen rows
 $6515 AND $F8       ;
 $6517 LD B,A        ;
 $6518 LD A,(HL)     ;
 $6519 ADD A,A       ;
 $651A OR B          ;
 $651B OR (HL)       ;
 $651C LD C,A        ;
 $651D SRL A         ;
 $651F AND $F8       ;
 $6521 LD B,A        ;
 $6522 LD A,C        ;
 $6523 ADD A,A       ;
 $6524 AND $0F       ;
 $6526 OR B          ;
 $6527 AND C         ;
 $6528 LD (DE),A     ;
 $6529 INC L         ;
 $652A INC D         ;
 $652B LD A,C        ;
 $652C LD (DE),A     ;
 $652D INC D         ; }
 $652E LD A,(HL)     ; {Row 1
 $652F RRCA          ;
 $6530 AND $F8       ;
 $6532 LD B,A        ;
 $6533 LD A,(HL)     ;
 $6534 ADD A,A       ;
 $6535 OR B          ;
 $6536 OR (HL)       ;
 $6537 LD (DE),A     ;
 $6538 INC L         ;
 $6539 INC D         ;
 $653A LD (DE),A     ;
 $653B INC D         ; }
 $653C LD A,(HL)     ; {Row 2
 $653D RRCA          ;
 $653E AND $F8       ;
 $6540 LD B,A        ;
 $6541 LD A,(HL)     ;
 $6542 ADD A,A       ;
 $6543 OR B          ;
 $6544 OR (HL)       ;
 $6545 LD (DE),A     ;
 $6546 INC L         ;
 $6547 INC D         ;
 $6548 DEC D         ; }
 $6549 LD A,E        ; {Carry the destination across into the next screen third
 $654A ADD A,$20     ;
 $654C LD E,A        ;
 $654D LD A,D        ;
 $654E ADC A,$00     ;
 $6550 AND $F8       ;
 $6552 LD D,A        ; }
 $6553 LD A,(HL)     ; {Row 3
 $6554 RRCA          ;
 $6555 AND $F8       ;
 $6557 LD B,A        ;
 $6558 LD A,(HL)     ;
 $6559 ADD A,A       ;
 $655A OR B          ;
 $655B OR (HL)       ;
 $655C LD (DE),A     ;
 $655D INC L         ;
 $655E INC D         ; }
 $655F LD A,(HL)     ; {Row 4
 $6560 RRCA          ;
 $6561 AND $F8       ;
 $6563 LD B,A        ;
 $6564 LD A,(HL)     ;
 $6565 ADD A,A       ;
 $6566 OR B          ;
 $6567 OR (HL)       ;
 $6568 LD (DE),A     ;
 $6569 INC L         ;
 $656A INC D         ;
 $656B LD (DE),A     ;
 $656C INC D         ; }
 $656D LD A,(HL)     ; {Row 5
 $656E RRCA          ;
 $656F AND $F8       ;
 $6571 LD B,A        ;
 $6572 LD A,(HL)     ;
 $6573 ADD A,A       ;
 $6574 OR B          ;
 $6575 OR (HL)       ;
 $6576 LD (DE),A     ;
 $6577 INC D         ; }
 $6578 LD C,A        ; {Row 6: narrower smear, masked so it cannot bleed into
 $6579 SRL A         ; the next cell
 $657B AND $F8       ;
 $657D LD B,A        ;
 $657E LD A,C        ;
 $657F ADD A,A       ;
 $6580 AND $1F       ;
 $6582 OR B          ;
 $6583 AND C         ;
 $6584 LD (DE),A     ;
 $6585 INC D         ; }
 $6586 XOR A         ; {Blank the four pixel rows below the glyph
 $6587 LD (DE),A     ;
 $6588 INC D         ;
 $6589 LD (DE),A     ;
 $658A INC D         ;
 $658B LD (DE),A     ; }
*$658C POP BC        ; {Restore BC/DE/HL/AF
 $658D POP DE        ;
 $658E POP HL        ;
 $658F POP AF        ; }
 $6590 LD ($9CCB),A  ; store last-printed char as new skip-print flag
 $6593 RET           ;
*$6594 CP $09        ; control-code path: codes >=9 treated as space
 $6596 JR NC,$65A9   ;
 $6598 ADD A,A       ; {Double the control code into a word offset
 $6599 LD E,A        ;
 $659A LD D,$00      ; }
 $659C LD HL,$65B3   ; dispatch via jump table #R$65B3
 $659F ADD HL,DE     ; {Fetch the handler address and enter it with $65A9
 $65A0 LD E,(HL)     ; pushed as its return
 $65A1 INC HL        ;
 $65A2 LD D,(HL)     ;
 $65A3 LD HL,$65A9   ;
 $65A6 PUSH HL       ;
 $65A7 EX DE,HL      ;
 $65A8 JP (HL)       ; }
*$65A9 LD A,$20      ; Codes $09 and above just count as a space
; This entry point is used by the routines at #R$65C5 and #R$65EA.
*$65AB LD ($9CCB),A  ; {Record it as the skip flag, restore and return
 $65AE POP BC        ;
 $65AF POP DE        ;
 $65B0 POP HL        ;
 $65B1 POP AF        ;
 $65B2 RET           ; }

; Control-code dispatch table (9 entries, codes 0-8, used by $6594)
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Control codes are two-byte escapes: printing a byte below $20 leaves it in
; $9CCB, and the next character #R$64CC receives is consumed as that code's
; parameter (in C) rather than being drawn. This table maps the code to its
; handler; codes $00 and $08 chain by discarding their return address and
; re-entering $65AB with a second code, so those take two parameter bytes.
; Anything from $09 up is treated as a space.
w$65B3 DEFW $65C5
 $65B5 DEFW $65D3
 $65B7 DEFW $65DC
 $65B9 DEFW $65F2
 $65BB DEFW $65FB
 $65BD DEFW $6612
 $65BF DEFW $6619
 $65C1 DEFW $65CE
 $65C3 DEFW $65EA

; Control code $00: set the top cell's colour, then chain into code $07
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Resets the cursor's row and skips ahead 7 characters, like a "start new row"
; print control code.
@label=pcc_set_colour_pair
c$65C5 LD HL,$9CC9   ; {zero the low byte of $9CC9 (cursor row reset)
 $65C8 LD (HL),C     ; }
 $65C9 LD A,$07      ; skip-count = 7
 $65CB POP HL        ; {discard pushed return address, jump into skip-flag
 $65CC JR $65AB      ; setter}

; Control code $07: set the bottom cell's colour ($9CCA)
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Simplest handler: just LD ($9CCA),C then return. $9CCA's purpose is not
; otherwise confirmed.
@label=pcc_set_colour2
c$65CE LD HL,$9CCA   ;
 $65D1 LD (HL),C     ;
 $65D2 RET           ;

; Control code $01: set the top cell's ink (bits 0-2 of $9CC9)
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Sets the print cursor's column (low 3 bits of $9CC9) from the control code's
; parameter.
@label=pcc_set_ink
c$65D3 LD HL,$9CC9   ;
 $65D6 LD A,(HL)     ;
 $65D7 AND $F8       ;
 $65D9 OR C          ; OR in code value (1) to low 3 bits of $9CC9
 $65DA LD (HL),A     ;
 $65DB RET           ;

; Control code $02: set the top cell's paper (bits 3-5 of $9CC9)
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Sets the print cursor's row (bits 3-5 of $9CC9) from the control code's
; parameter.
@label=pcc_set_paper
c$65DC LD HL,$9CC9   ;
 $65DF LD A,C        ;
 $65E0 ADD A,A       ;
 $65E1 ADD A,A       ;
 $65E2 ADD A,A       ;
 $65E3 LD C,A        ;
 $65E4 LD A,(HL)     ;
 $65E5 AND $C7       ;
 $65E7 OR C          ; OR in code value<<3 to bits 3-5 of $9CC9
 $65E8 LD (HL),A     ;
 $65E9 RET           ;

; Control code $08: set the column via code $03, then chain into code $04
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Runs control code $03's conversion, then arms a 4-character skip count.
@label=pcc_set_column_addr
c$65EA CALL $65F2    ; Control code $03
 $65ED LD A,$04      ; skip-count = 4
 $65EF POP HL        ;
 $65F0 JR $65AB      ;

; Control code $03: set the cursor column (bits 0-4 of #R$9CC7)
;
; Used by the routine at #R$65EA.
;
; .
;
; Shared: also called by control code $08 with C=8 instead of 3.
@label=pcc_set_column
c$65F2 LD HL,$9CC7   ;
 $65F5 LD A,(HL)     ;
 $65F6 AND $E0       ;
 $65F8 OR C          ; OR C into bits 0-4 of #R$9CC7
 $65F9 LD (HL),A     ;
 $65FA RET           ;

; Control code $04: fold the row into #R$9CC7 and convert it to a screen
; address
;
; Used by the routine at #R$6619.
;
; .
;
; Shared: also reached from control code $06 with a different C value. Converts
; the cursor field #R$9CC7 into a screen pixel address (same bit-twiddle as
; #R$64CC's blit), folding in C.
@label=pcc_cursor_to_addr
c$65FB LD HL,($9CC7) ; {Rotate C into the row-third bits
 $65FE LD A,C        ;
 $65FF RRCA          ;
 $6600 RRCA          ;
 $6601 RRCA          ;
 $6602 LD C,A        ; }
 $6603 AND $03       ; {Fold in the screen-third base ($58xx)
 $6605 OR $58        ;
 $6607 LD H,A        ; }
 $6608 LD A,C        ; {Combine column and row bits into the low byte
 $6609 XOR L         ;
 $660A AND $E0       ;
 $660C XOR L         ;
 $660D LD L,A        ; }
 $660E LD ($9CC7),HL ; store converted pixel address back into #R$9CC7
 $6611 RET           ;

; Control code $05: advance the cursor by the parameter
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Nudges the print position along by the control code's parameter.
@label=pcc_advance_cursor
c$6612 LD HL,$9CC7   ;
 $6615 LD A,(HL)     ;
 $6616 ADD A,C       ; add code value (5) to low byte of #R$9CC7
 $6617 LD (HL),A     ;
 $6618 RET           ;

; Control code $06: derive the row from #R$9CC7, then reuse code $04's
; conversion
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Rescales the cursor field into a column index, folds in the control code's
; parameter, and reuses code $04's address conversion.
@label=pcc_set_row
c$6619 LD HL,($9CC7) ;
 $661C ADD HL,HL     ;
 $661D ADD HL,HL     ;
 $661E ADD HL,HL     ;
 $661F LD A,H        ;
 $6620 AND $1F       ; {mask to 5 bits, add code value (6)
 $6622 ADD A,C       ; }
 $6623 LD C,A        ;
 $6624 JR $65FB      ; reuse control code $04's conversion with this C

; Print string (control codes + ROM-font text) from HL
;
; Used by the routines at #R$6648 and #R$A6E5.
;
; HL pointer to $FF-terminated string
;
; Prints a $FF-terminated string, treating bytes below $20 as control codes
; (position/attribute changes) rather than characters.
@label=print_string
c$6626 PUSH AF       ; {save AF/HL
 $6627 PUSH HL       ; }
*$6628 LD A,($9CCB)  ; check skip-print flag at $9CCB
 $662B CP $20        ;
 $662D LD A,(HL)     ; {read next byte, advance HL; branch if control code
 $662E INC HL        ; (<$20)
 $662F JR C,$6639    ; }
 $6631 CP $FF        ; check string terminator $FF
 $6633 JR Z,$6645    ; exit if string terminated
 $6635 CP $1B        ; {check position/attribute control code $1B
 $6637 JR Z,$663E    ; }
*$6639 CALL $64CC    ; Print character to screen using ROM font
 $663C JR $6628      ; loop for next character
*$663E LD A,(HL)     ; {read control parameter byte, apply via #R$6648
 $663F INC HL        ;
 $6640 CALL $6648    ; }
 $6643 JR $6628      ; loop back
*$6645 POP HL        ; {restore AF/HL and return
 $6646 POP AF        ;
 $6647 RET           ; }

; Print message N from table $627A
;
; Used by the routines at #R$6498, #R$6626, #R$67C7, #R$67F1, #R$6989, #R$6A6D,
; #R$6A88, #R$A6BB, #R$A6E5, #R$A783 and #R$A802.
;
; A message number (0-based) to print
;
; Looks up a message by its number and prints it via #R$6626.
@label=print_message
c$6648 PUSH AF       ; {save AF/HL/DE/BC
 $6649 PUSH HL       ;
 $664A PUSH DE       ;
 $664B PUSH BC       ; }
 $664C LD HL,$627A   ; point HL at string index table #R$627A
 $664F LD E,A        ; {init search count E=A+1, set terminator byte $FF
 $6650 INC E         ;
 $6651 LD A,$FF      ; }
 $6653 LD B,A        ; {search table for the (A+1)th $FF-terminated string
*$6654 CPIR          ; using CPIR}
 $6656 DEC E         ; {loop until count exhausted
 $6657 JR NZ,$6654   ; }
 $6659 CALL $6626    ; Print string (control codes + ROM-font text) from HL
 $665C POP BC        ; {restore AF/HL/DE/BC
 $665D POP DE        ;
 $665E POP HL        ;
 $665F POP AF        ; }
 $6660 RET           ; return

; Unused
s$6661 DEFB $3E,$20

; Print packed-BCD number with leading-zero suppression
;
; Used by the routines at #R$66DE and #R$A6E5.
;
; HL pointer to 3-byte packed-BCD value
; A fill character for suppressed leading zeros ($FE = pad remainder with
; . spaces instead)
;
; Copies the BCD value to scratch ($9C2B), then unpacks its 6 nibbles via RLD
; (one per digit), printing each through #R$64CC; nibbles that are still zero
; before the first nonzero digit print the fill character A instead of "0". If
; A was $FE on entry, once all 6 digits are printed it pads the unused width
; with spaces (count = original 6 minus digits actually printed, tracked in D).
@label=print_bcd_number
c$6663 PUSH AF       ;
 $6664 LD DE,$9C2B   ; copy source BCD value to scratch $9C2B
 $6667 LD BC,$0003   ;
 $666A LDIR          ;
 $666C LD C,A        ; C = fill character (from entry A)
 $666D PUSH HL       ;
 $666E LD HL,$9C2B   ;
 $6671 LD D,$00      ;
 $6673 LD B,$05      ;
 $6675 LD A,$0F      ;
*$6677 RLD           ; unpack next BCD digit (RLD)
 $6679 CP $0F        ;
 $667B JR NZ,$6680   ;
 $667D INC HL        ;
 $667E RLD           ;
*$6680 LD E,A        ;
 $6681 AND A         ;
 $6682 JR Z,$6687    ;
 $6684 INC B         ;
 $6685 JR $669A      ;
*$6687 LD A,C        ; leading zero: print fill character instead of digit
 $6688 CALL $64CC    ; Print character to screen using ROM font
 $668B INC D         ;
 $668C LD A,E        ;
 $668D DJNZ $6677    ;
 $668F INC B         ;
*$6690 RLD           ;
 $6692 CP $0F        ;
 $6694 JR NZ,$6699   ;
 $6696 INC HL        ;
 $6697 RLD           ;
*$6699 LD E,A        ;
*$669A ADD A,$30     ;
 $669C CALL $64CC    ; Print character to screen using ROM font
 $669F LD A,E        ;
 $66A0 DJNZ $6690    ;
 $66A2 RLD           ;
 $66A4 POP HL        ;
 $66A5 POP AF        ;
 $66A6 CP $FE        ; check for space-padding mode (A=$FE)
 $66A8 RET NZ        ;
 $66A9 LD A,D        ;
 $66AA AND A         ;
 $66AB RET Z         ;
 $66AC LD B,A        ; B = remaining width to pad
 $66AD LD A,$20      ;
*$66AF CALL $64CC    ; Print character to screen using ROM font
 $66B2 DJNZ $66AF    ;
 $66B4 RET           ;

; Add BCD score value to current player's score
;
; Used by the routines at #R$A802, #R$C075, #R$C11C, #R$C199, #R$C217, #R$C298,
; #R$C31A, #R$C388, #R$C3C7 and #R$C5D2.
;
; A table index into $A094 (0=use HL directly)
; HL score value to add, when A=0
;
; Adds a 3-byte packed-BCD value to the active player's score field ($9C7B for
; player 1, $9C87 for player 2, selected via $9C76), then sets bit 1 of $9C27
; (likely a "score changed, redraw HUD" flag). If A=0 the value is added
; directly from HL; otherwise A indexes a table of preset score values at $A094
; (3 bytes per entry).
@label=add_score
c$66B5 AND A         ; {if A=0 use HL as score value directly; else point HL at
 $66B6 LD HL,$A094   ; score-value table $A094
 $66B9 JR Z,$66C2    ; }
 $66BB LD B,A        ; {index into table: HL += 3*A
 $66BC LD DE,$0003   ;
*$66BF ADD HL,DE     ;
 $66C0 DJNZ $66BF    ; }
*$66C2 LD DE,$9C7B   ; {point DE at player 1 score field; check active player
 $66C5 LD A,($9C76)  ;
 $66C8 DEC A         ;
 $66C9 JR Z,$66CE    ; }
 $66CB LD DE,$9C87   ; player 2: point DE at player 2 score field instead
*$66CE LD B,$03      ; 3-byte BCD add loop count
*$66D0 LD A,(DE)     ; {add BCD byte with carry, store back, advance pointers,
 $66D1 ADC A,(HL)    ; repeat for 3 bytes
 $66D2 DAA           ;
 $66D3 LD (DE),A     ;
 $66D4 DEC HL        ;
 $66D5 DEC DE        ;
 $66D6 DJNZ $66D0    ; }
 $66D8 LD HL,$9C27   ; {set score-changed/redraw flag at $9C27
 $66DB SET 1,(HL)    ; }
 $66DD RET           ; return

; Print a player's score at its HUD position
;
; Used by the routines at #R$6498, #R$6771, #R$A178 and #R$A802.
;
; A player number (1 or 2)
;
; Selects the score cursor coordinates ($9C1D/$9C1F, active vs. other player
; via $9C76) and the score data pointer (player 1: $9C79/fill=$FE space-pad;
; player 2: $9C85/fill=$20 plain space), sets the print cursor (#R$9CC7/$9CC9),
; then calls #R$6663 to print the BCD score.
@label=print_player_score
c$66DE PUSH AF       ;
 $66DF LD HL,$9C76   ; compare entry player number to active player ($9C76)
 $66E2 CP (HL)       ;
 $66E3 LD BC,($9C1D) ;
 $66E7 JR Z,$66ED    ;
 $66E9 LD BC,($9C1F) ; other player: use $9C1F cursor coordinate
*$66ED CP $01        ; is this player 1?
 $66EF LD HL,$9C79   ;
 $66F2 LD DE,($9C21) ;
 $66F6 LD A,$FE      ; player 1: fill character = $FE (space-pad)
 $66F8 JR Z,$6703    ;
 $66FA LD HL,$9C85   ;
 $66FD LD DE,($9C23) ;
 $6701 LD A,$20      ; player 2: fill character = $20 (plain space)
*$6703 LD ($9CC7),DE ; set print cursor column (#R$9CC7)
 $6707 LD ($9CC9),BC ; set print cursor row ($9CC9)
 $670B PUSH HL       ; {IX = score data pointer
 $670C POP IX        ; }
 $670E LD DE,$0000   ;
 $6711 ADD HL,DE     ;
 $6712 CALL $6663    ; Print packed-BCD number with leading-zero suppression
 $6715 POP AF        ;
 $6716 RET           ;

; Compare 3 bytes at (DE) vs (HL); NC if all equal
;
; Used by the routine at #R$6989.
;
;   DE,HL pointers to the two 3-byte sequences
; O:Cy set if any byte differs, clear if all 3 match
;
; Checks whether two 3-character sequences match, such as a player's initials
; against a high-score entry.
c$6717 PUSH HL       ;
 $6718 PUSH DE       ;
 $6719 PUSH BC       ;
 $671A LD B,$03      ;
*$671C LD A,(DE)     ; {Compare a byte pair
 $671D CP (HL)       ; }
 $671E JR Z,$6722    ; Bail out on first mismatch
 $6720 JR $6727      ;
*$6722 INC DE        ;
 $6723 INC HL        ;
 $6724 DJNZ $671C    ; Loop the 3 bytes
 $6726 SCF           ; All matched: flag equal (SCF)
*$6727 CCF           ; Invert so carry = "differs"
 $6728 POP BC        ;
 $6729 POP DE        ;
 $672A POP HL        ;
 $672B RET           ;

; Draw icon row: up to 6 filled cells (colour C), rest blank

; Used by the routine at #R$672C.

; writing both attribute rows so each icon is two cells tall.
@label=draw_icon_row

 $6752 LD B,A        ; }
 $6753 CP $08        ; {Clamp filled cells to max 6
 $6755 JR C,$6759    ; }
 $6757 LD B,$06      ;
*$6759 AND A         ;
 $675A LD A,$06      ; {Blank count = 6 - filled
 $675C JR Z,$6769    ;
 $675E SUB B         ; }

 $6762 LD (IY+$20),C ; IY+$20)}
 $6765 INC IY        ;

*$6769 LD B,A        ; {Switch to blank cells (colour 0)
 $676A LD C,$00      ;
 $676C AND A         ; }
 $676D LD A,C        ;
 $676E JR NZ,$675F   ; Loop blank cells
 $6770 RET           ;
