; Paint attribute colour-wipe column (menu highlight effect)
;
; Used by the routines at #R$6989, #R$6A6D, #R$A6E5 and #R$A783.
;
; A row/column count (used as both position and loop count B)
; C flags (bit 7: special mode, unconfirmed)
; E screen column
;
; Paints a 2-row-tall column of screen attributes at (row A, col E) with bytes
; from a repeating $FF-terminated sequence at $9CCC, B columns wide, synced to
; HALT and interruptible by fire. Looks like a colour-wipe/highlight-bar effect
; (e.g. for menu selection); exact meaning of the high/low bits of C is
; unconfirmed.
@label=paint_wipe_column
c$6778 LD B,A        ; {B=column count; compute row pixel offset from A
 $6779 SRL A         ;
 $677B NEG           ;
 $677D ADD A,$10     ; }
 $677F LD L,A        ; {start attribute address calc from column E
 $6780 LD A,E        ;
 $6781 RRCA          ;
 $6782 RRCA          ;
 $6783 RRCA          ; }
 $6784 LD H,A        ; {combine row/column bits into attribute address
 $6785 AND $E0       ;
 $6787 OR L          ;
 $6788 LD L,A        ;
 $6789 LD A,H        ;
 $678A AND $1F       ; }
 $678C ADD A,$58     ; {add attribute-memory base, store into IX
 $678E LD H,A        ; }
 $678F PUSH HL       ; {load computed attribute address into IX
 $6790 POP IX        ; }
 $6792 LD DE,$9CCC   ; {DE=pointer into repeating colour sequence;
 $6795 LD HL,$9CDE   ; HL=fire-debounce flag}
*$6798 HALT          ; sync to frame
 $6799 BIT 7,C       ; check special-mode flag in C
 $679B JR NZ,$67A5   ; skip input poll if special mode
 $679D CALL $68B1    ; Read input
 $67A0 LD A,($9CDC)  ; {check fire pressed
 $67A3 OR (HL)       ; }
 $67A4 RET NZ        ; return if fire pressed
*$67A5 HALT          ; sync to frame
 $67A6 LD A,(DE)     ; {read next colour byte, check sequence terminator $FF
 $67A7 INC DE        ;
 $67A8 CP $FF        ; }
 $67AA JR NZ,$67B0   ; skip wrap if not terminated
 $67AC LD DE,$9CCC   ; wrap sequence pointer to start
 $67AF LD A,(DE)     ; reload first colour byte after wrap
*$67B0 PUSH BC       ; {save loop state
 $67B1 PUSH IX       ; }
*$67B3 LD (IX+$00),A ; {paint attribute cell and the cell 4 rows below (32-byte
 $67B6 LD (IX+$20),A ; stride)}
 $67B9 INC IX        ; advance to next column
 $67BB DJNZ $67B3    ; repeat for B columns
 $67BD POP IX        ; {restore loop state
 $67BF POP BC        ; }
 $67C0 LD A,C        ; {mask special-mode flag off C
 $67C1 AND $7F       ; }
 $67C3 RET Z         ;
 $67C4 DEC C         ;
 $67C5 JR $6798      ;

; Redefine keys: prompt for and store each direction/fire key
;
; Used by the routine at #R$6A4A.
;
; .
;
; Loops 5 times (E=$0A..$0E), printing the "FIRE"/"UP"/"DOWN"/"LEFT"/"RIGHT"
; labels via #R$6648, waiting for a keypress via #R$6829/#R$686A (keyboard scan
; with animated highlight), then storing the chosen key's row/mask (B,C) into
; the redefinable-key table at $9CE0 - the same table #R$68B1 reads when
; decoding keyboard input.
@label=redefine_keys
c$67C7 PUSH AF       ;
 $67C8 LD A,$09      ;
 $67CA LD B,$05      ;
 $67CC LD E,A        ;
 $67CD LD HL,$9CE0   ;
*$67D0 PUSH BC       ;
 $67D1 INC E         ;
 $67D2 LD A,E        ;
 $67D3 CALL $6648    ; Print message N from table $627A
 $67D6 LD C,(HL)     ;
 $67D7 INC HL        ;
 $67D8 LD B,(HL)     ;
 $67D9 CALL $67F1    ; Print a redefined key's name
 $67DC CALL $6829    ; Scan keyboard for a keypress
 $67DF CALL $67F1    ; Print a redefined key's name
*$67E2 CALL $686A    ; Copy 16 bytes from wrapping sequence ($9C25) into screen
                     ; at $5A68
 $67E5 JR NC,$67E2   ;
 $67E7 LD (HL),B     ;
 $67E8 DEC HL        ;
 $67E9 LD (HL),C     ;
 $67EA INC HL        ;
 $67EB INC HL        ;
 $67EC POP BC        ;
 $67ED DJNZ $67D0    ;
 $67EF POP AF        ;
 $67F0 RET           ;

; Print a redefined key's name (character or CS/SS/SP/EN)
;
; Used by the routine at #R$67C7.
;
; B key bit mask within its half-row (as read from the $9CE0 pairs)
; C half-row port value for that key
; AF,HL,BC preserved; the print cursor #R$9CC7 is saved and restored
;
; Prints the name of one redefined key: the key's bit position within its
; keyboard half-row is found by shifting, and the resulting code either selects
; a name message for the four special keys (CAPS SHIFT, SYMBOL SHIFT, SPACE,
; ENTER) or is printed directly as a character. The print cursor is saved and
; restored around it so callers can lay keys out in a table.
@label=print_key_name
c$67F1 PUSH AF       ; {Save AF/HL/BC
 $67F2 PUSH HL       ;
 $67F3 PUSH BC       ; }
 $67F4 LD A,$FB      ; {Count the key's half-row: +5 per set bit rotated out of
*$67F6 ADD A,$05     ; C
 $67F8 RR C          ;
 $67FA JR C,$67F6    ; }
 $67FC DEC A         ; {Add the key's bit position within that half-row,
*$67FD INC A         ; scanning B
 $67FE RR B          ;
 $6800 JR NC,$67FD   ; }
 $6802 LD C,A        ; {Index the redefined-key table at $9CF0 by that flat key
 $6803 LD B,$00      ; number
 $6805 LD HL,$9CF0   ;
 $6808 ADD HL,BC     ; }
 $6809 LD A,(HL)     ; Fetch the key's code
 $680A LD BC,($9CC7) ; Save the print cursor ($9CC7)
 $680E CP $04        ; {Codes 0-3 are the four special keys; anything else
 $6810 JR NC,$6819   ; prints as a character}
 $6812 ADD A,$06     ; map key-code 0-3 to message $06-$09 (CS/SS/SP/EN)
 $6814 CALL $6648    ; Print message N from table $627A
 $6817 JR $681C      ; Skip the character path
*$6819 CALL $64CC    ; Print character to screen using ROM font
*$681C LD A,$20      ; Follow the name with a space
 $681E CALL $64CC    ; Print character to screen using ROM font
 $6821 LD ($9CC7),BC ; Restore the print cursor
 $6825 POP BC        ; {Restore AF/HL/BC and return
 $6826 POP HL        ;
 $6827 POP AF        ;
 $6828 RET           ; }

; Scan keyboard for a keypress (animated wait, debounced)
;
; Used by the routine at #R$67C7.
;
; O:B,C row/mask of the key pressed
;
; Waits for a keypress while animating the screen, scanning the six keyboard
; half-rows listed at $9CEA until exactly one key is down. It then waits for
; that key to be released before returning, so a single press cannot be read
; twice.
@label=wait_keypress
c$6829 PUSH AF       ; {Save AF/HL/DE
 $682A PUSH HL       ;
 $682B PUSH DE       ; }
 $682C CALL $6861    ; Reset animated-sequence pointer
*$682F CALL $686A    ; Copy 16 bytes from wrapping sequence ($9C25) into screen
                     ; at $5A68
 $6832 LD HL,$9CEA   ; {Point at the half-row port table ($9CEA); scan 6
 $6835 LD B,$06      ; half-rows}
*$6837 LD A,(HL)     ; {Read this half-row, invert and mask to its 5 key bits
 $6838 IN A,($FE)    ;
 $683A CPL           ;
 $683B AND $1F       ; }
 $683D JR Z,$6846    ; Nothing pressed here: move on to the next half-row
 $683F LD C,A        ; {Isolate the lowest set bit; a non-zero remainder means
*$6840 SRL A         ; 2+ keys are down
 $6842 JR NC,$6840   ; }
 $6844 JR Z,$684B    ; Exactly one key down: accept it
*$6846 INC HL        ; {Next half-row
 $6847 DJNZ $6837    ; }
 $6849 JR $682F      ; All 6 scanned with nothing valid: animate a frame and
                     ; rescan
*$684B LD B,C        ; {B = key bit mask, C = its half-row port (the pair
 $684C LD C,(HL)     ; #R$67F1 decodes)}
*$684D CALL $686A    ; Copy 16 bytes from wrapping sequence ($9C25) into screen
                     ; at $5A68
 $6850 XOR A         ; {Read every half-row at once; keep animating until all
 $6851 IN A,($FE)    ; keys are released
 $6853 CPL           ;
 $6854 AND $1F       ;
 $6856 JR NZ,$684D   ; }
*$6858 CALL $686A    ; Copy 16 bytes from wrapping sequence ($9C25) into screen
                     ; at $5A68
 $685B JR NC,$6858   ; Keep animating until the colour sequence wraps ($686A
                     ; returns carry set)
 $685D POP DE        ; {Restore AF/HL/DE and return
 $685E POP HL        ;
 $685F POP AF        ;
 $6860 RET           ; }

; Reset animated-sequence pointer ($9C25 = $9CCC)
;
; Used by the routine at #R$6829.
;
; .
;
; Rewinds the animated colour sequence back to its start ($9CCC).
c$6861 PUSH HL       ;
 $6862 LD HL,$9CCC   ;
 $6865 LD ($9C25),HL ;
 $6868 POP HL        ;
 $6869 RET           ;

; Copy 16 bytes from wrapping sequence ($9C25) into screen at $5A68
;
; Used by the routines at #R$67C7 and #R$6829.
;
; O:F carry set when the sequence hit its $FF terminator and wrapped
; O:A corrupted; BC,DE,HL,IX preserved
;
; Waits 2 frames, then copies B=16 bytes from the repeating $FF-terminated
; sequence at $9CCC (tracked via pointer $9C25, same source used by #R$6778's
; colour-wipe effect), wrapping back to the start on the terminator, into a
; fixed screen destination at $5A68.
c$686A HALT          ; {Wait 2 frames
 $686B HALT          ; }
 $686C PUSH BC       ;
 $686D PUSH DE       ;
 $686E PUSH IX       ;
 $6870 LD IX,$5A68   ;
 $6874 LD DE,($9C25) ; DE = sequence cursor ($9C25)
 $6878 LD B,$10      ; Copy 16 bytes
 $687A LD A,(DE)     ;
 $687B INC DE        ;
 $687C CP $FF        ; On $FF terminator, wrap to sequence start
 $687E CCF           ;
 $687F JR NZ,$6885   ;
 $6881 LD DE,$9CCC   ; {Reload cursor to $9CCC
 $6884 LD A,(DE)     ; }
*$6885 LD (IX+$00),A ; {Write byte to two rows ($5A68 and +$20)
 $6888 LD (IX+$20),A ; }
 $688B INC IX        ;
 $688D DJNZ $6885    ;
 $688F LD ($9C25),DE ; Save advanced cursor back to $9C25
 $6893 POP IX        ;
 $6895 POP DE        ;
 $6896 POP BC        ;
 $6897 RET           ;

; Wait up to N frames, exit early on fire
;
; .
;
; A number of frames to wait
;
; Waits up to A frames, returning early if fire is pressed.
@label=wait_frames_or_fire

 $68A0 LD B,A        ;
*$68A1 HALT          ;
 $68A2 CALL $68B1    ; Read input
 $68A5 LD A,($9CDC)  ; {check fire pressed
 $68A8 CP $01        ; }

 $68AD DJNZ $68A1    ;
*$68AF POP BC        ;
 $68B0 RET           ;

; Read input (Kempston or keyboard)
;
; Used by the routines at #R$6778, #R$689F, #R$6971, #R$6989 and #R$BE03.
;
; O:$9CDC fire-hold count (incremented while fire is down, 0 on release)
; O:$9CDD $FF on a fire press or release edge
; O:$9CDE direction bits, fire bit stripped
;   AF,HL,DE,BC all preserved
;
; Reads the player's controls into a single direction+fire byte, merging three
; input sources: the Kempston joystick (if enabled), the fixed CAPS SHIFT
; direction keys, and the user's redefined keys. It also watches for the
; fire+redefine combo that toggles the redefine mode, debounced so one press
; registers once.
@label=read_input
c$68B1 PUSH AF       ; {Save AF/HL/DE/BC
 $68B2 PUSH HL       ;
 $68B3 PUSH DE       ;
 $68B4 PUSH BC       ; }
 $68B5 LD C,$00      ; {init direction accumulator C=0, loop counter B=5
 $68B7 LD B,$05      ; }
 $68B9 LD HL,$9CE0   ; Point at the redefined-key table ($9CE0): 5 x [half-row
                     ; port, key mask]
; Reads Kempston joystick (port $1F) and keyboard (port $FE) into shift
; register at $9CE0-$9CE1.
*$68BC LD A,(HL)     ; {Read this key's half-row and mask it down to that key's
 $68BD INC HL        ; bit
 $68BE IN A,($FE)    ;
 $68C0 AND (HL)      ; }
 $68C1 CP $01        ; {shift key state bit into C
 $68C3 RL C          ; }
 $68C5 INC HL        ; {Next key pair
 $68C6 DJNZ $68BC    ; }
 $68C8 LD HL,$9CDF   ; check Kempston-enabled flag at $9CDF
 $68CB BIT 0,(HL)    ; {Kempston not enabled: fall through to the keyboard
 $68CD JR Z,$68D7    ; }
 $68CF IN A,($1F)    ; read Kempston joystick
 $68D1 AND $1F       ;
 $68D3 SET 0,(HL)    ; mark Kempston active
 $68D5 JR $691E      ; Kempston reading is the whole answer
*$68D7 LD A,$EF      ; {read CAPS SHIFT+direction keys (port $FE row $EF)
 $68D9 IN A,($FE)    ; }
 $68DB CPL           ; {Invert and mask to the row's 5 key bits
 $68DC AND $1F       ;
 $68DE LD E,A        ; }
 $68DF LD A,$F7      ; read SPACE+redefine keys (port $FE row $F7)
 $68E1 IN A,($FE)    ; Read the SPACE/redefine half-row
 $68E3 BIT 1,E       ; {skip redefine-toggle if not held
 $68E5 JR NZ,$690B   ; }
 $68E7 BIT 1,(HL)    ; {Combo already debounced: treat as a normal read
 $68E9 JR NZ,$690B   ; }
*$68EB RES 1,(HL)    ; clear redefine-toggle debounce flag
 $68ED BIT 4,A       ; {fire button from row $EF bit 4
 $68EF JR NZ,$68F3   ; }
 $68F1 SET 1,B       ; Fire held: set bit 1 of the output byte (B, free now the
                     ; scan loop ended)
*$68F3 LD A,E        ; {decode direction bits from E into B
 $68F4 RRCA          ;
 $68F5 JR NC,$68F9   ;
 $68F7 SET 4,B       ; }
*$68F9 RRCA          ; {Shift the remaining direction bits out of E into the
 $68FA RRCA          ; output byte
 $68FB JR NC,$68FE   ;
 $68FD INC B         ;
*$68FE RRCA          ;
 $68FF JR NC,$6903   ;
 $6901 SET 3,B       ;
*$6903 RRCA          ;
 $6904 JR NC,$6908   ;
 $6906 SET 2,B       ; }
*$6908 LD A,B        ; {return combined direction+fire byte
 $6909 JR $691E      ; }
*$690B BIT 4,A       ; check fire+redefine combo held
 $690D JR Z,$68EB    ; Fire not also held: not the combo, treat as a normal
                     ; read
 $690F SET 1,(HL)    ; set redefine-toggle debounce flag
 $6911 XOR A         ; {encode redefined-key row into direction bits
 $6912 SRL E         ;
 $6914 RLA           ;
 $6915 SRL E         ;
 $6917 RLA           ;
 $6918 SRL E         ;
 $691A RLA           ;
 $691B RLCA          ;
 $691C RLCA          ;
 $691D OR E          ; }
*$691E OR C          ; {combine keyboard bits with accumulator
 $691F LD C,A        ; }
 $6920 LD HL,$9CDC   ; {E = previous fire-hold count; A = one more
 $6923 LD A,(HL)     ;
 $6924 LD E,A        ;
 $6925 INC A         ; }
 $6926 BIT 4,C       ; {Fire still down? otherwise reset the count to zero
 $6928 JR NZ,$692B   ;
 $692A XOR A         ; }
*$692B LD (HL),A     ; {Store the new fire-hold count ($9CDC), drop the fire
 $692C RES 4,C       ; bit from C}
 $692E LD D,A        ; {D = $FF when fire is down now
 $692F XOR A         ;
 $6930 CP D          ;
 $6931 SBC A,A       ;
 $6932 LD D,A        ; }
 $6933 XOR A         ; {A = $FF when fire was down before; XOR leaves $FF only
 $6934 CP E          ; on a press or release edge ($9CDD)
 $6935 SBC A,A       ;
 $6936 XOR D         ;
 $6937 LD ($9CDD),A  ; }
 $693A LD HL,$9CDE   ; {Store the direction bits ($9CDE)
 $693D LD (HL),C     ; }
 $693E POP BC        ; {Restore BC/DE/HL/AF and return
 $693F POP DE        ;
 $6940 POP HL        ;
 $6941 POP AF        ;
 $6942 RET           ; }

; Read fire button (Kempston/keyboard) with debounce
;
; Used by the routines at #R$A6BB, #R$A6E5, #R$A8A7 and #R$A94C.
;
; O:Cy fire button pressed
;
; Reads Kempston joystick fire button (port $1F, bit 4) combined with keyboard
; debounce (port $FE); returns pressed state in carry flag.
@label=read_fire
c$6943 PUSH HL       ;
 $6944 PUSH BC       ;
 $6945 LD HL,$9CDF   ; {save and set debounce flag at $9CDF
 $6948 LD C,(HL)     ;
 $6949 SET 0,(HL)    ; }
 $694B IN A,($1F)    ; read Kempston joystick fire
 $694D AND $1F       ;
 $694F CP $10        ;
 $6951 JR Z,$696E    ; skip if Kempston fire not pressed
 $6953 RES 0,(HL)    ; {clear debounce flag, point to keyboard debounce mask
 $6955 LD HL,$9CE0   ; }
 $6958 LD A,(HL)     ;
 $6959 INC HL        ;
 $695A IN A,($FE)    ; read keyboard, compare against debounce mask
 $695C AND (HL)      ;
 $695D JR Z,$696E    ; skip if key not held
 $695F LD A,$EF      ; {read keyboard row $EF (SPACE bar)
 $6961 IN A,($FE)    ; }
 $6963 RRA           ;
 $6964 JR NC,$696E   ;
 $6966 LD HL,$9CDF   ; restore debounce flag if fire release confirmed
 $6969 LD (HL),C     ;
 $696A AND A         ;
*$696B POP BC        ;
 $696C POP HL        ;
 $696D RET           ;
*$696E SCF           ;
 $696F JR $696B      ;

; Wait for input (debounced, up to 3 frames)
;
; Used by the routines at #R$6989, #R$A773 and #R$A8C0.
;
; AF,HL,BC preserved (DE untouched); returns once the controls read clear for 3
; .        frames
;
; Waits for all controls to be released, requiring them to stay clear for 3
; consecutive frames so a held key does not carry over.
@label=wait_for_input
c$6971 PUSH AF       ;
 $6972 PUSH HL       ;
 $6973 PUSH BC       ;
 $6974 LD HL,$9CDE   ;
*$6977 LD B,$03      ;
*$6979 HALT          ;
 $697A CALL $68B1    ; Read input
 $697D LD A,($9CDC)  ; get Input state / action code
 $6980 OR (HL)       ;
 $6981 JR NZ,$6977   ;
 $6983 DJNZ $6979    ;
 $6985 POP BC        ;
 $6986 POP HL        ;
 $6987 POP AF        ;
 $6988 RET           ;

; High-score entry: check the score, shuffle the table and type in initials
;
; Used by the routine at #R$A783.
;
; .
;
; Returns straight away unless the player's score beats one of the six
; high-score entries. Otherwise it congratulates them, shuffles the table down
; to open a slot, and runs the initials-entry screen where up/down cycle each
; letter through A-Z and fire accepts it.
@label=check_high_score
c$6989 CALL $6971    ; Wait for input
 $698C LD HL,($9C77) ; {IX and DE point at the player's score record ($9C77)
 $698F PUSH HL       ;
 $6990 POP IX        ;
 $6992 LD DE,$0000   ;
 $6995 ADD HL,DE     ;
 $6996 EX DE,HL      ; }
 $6997 LD HL,$6240   ; {Point at the high-score table ($6240); 6 entries
 $699A LD B,$06      ; }
*$699C CALL $6717    ; Compare 3 bytes at (DE) vs
 $699F JR C,$69AA    ; Score beats this entry: go and insert it
 $69A1 PUSH BC       ; {Otherwise step on to the next entry (11 bytes each)
 $69A2 LD BC,$000B   ;
 $69A5 ADD HL,BC     ;
 $69A6 POP BC        ; }
 $69A7 DJNZ $699C    ; {Loop 6 entries; return if the score beat none of them
 $69A9 RET           ; }
*$69AA PUSH HL       ; {Save the beaten entry's address and the player's score
 $69AB PUSH DE       ; pointer}
 $69AC LD A,$05      ; "CONGRATULATIONS!...A GREAT SCORE...???"
 $69AE CALL $6648    ; Print message N from table $627A
 $69B1 LD DE,$0000   ; {Point at entry 5's name field ($6272); the first copy
 $69B4 LD HL,$6272   ; goes to $0000 and is discarded}
*$69B7 PUSH HL       ; {Copy this entry's 8-byte name/position field down into
 $69B8 PUSH BC       ; the entry below
 $69B9 LD BC,$0008   ;
 $69BC LDIR          ;
 $69BE POP BC        ;
 $69BF POP DE        ; }
 $69C0 LD HL,$FFF5   ; {Step back to the previous entry (-$0B)
 $69C3 ADD HL,DE     ;
 $69C4 DJNZ $69B7    ; }
 $69C6 POP HL        ; {Recover the insert position and the player's score
 $69C7 POP DE        ; }
 $69C8 LD BC,$0003   ; {Copy the player's 3-byte score into the freed slot
 $69CB LDIR          ; }
 $69CD LD HL,$FFF8   ; {Back up 8 bytes to that entry's name field
 $69D0 ADD HL,DE     ; }
 $69D1 LD IX,$59CE   ; {IX = screen position, IY = initials buffer ($9CC4); 3
 $69D5 LD IY,$9CC4   ; letters to enter
 $69D9 LD B,$03      ; }
*$69DB PUSH BC       ; {Save the letter counter
 $69DC LD C,(IY+$00) ; }
 $69DF EX AF,AF'     ; {Arm the auto-accept timeout (100 ticks, held in shadow
 $69E0 LD A,$64      ; A)
 $69E2 EX AF,AF'     ; }
*$69E3 LD ($9CC7),IX ; {Set the print cursor and load the letter being edited
 $69E7 LD A,C        ; }
 $69E8 CALL $64CC    ; Print character to screen using ROM font
 $69EB CALL $68B1    ; Read input
 $69EE LD A,($9CDC)  ; get Input state / action code
 $69F1 AND A         ; {Fire pressed: accept this letter
 $69F2 JR NZ,$6A2C   ; }
 $69F4 LD A,$05      ; Wait 5 frames between repeats
 $69F6 CALL $6898    ; Wait N frames
 $69F9 EX AF,AF'     ; {Time the letter out once the 100 ticks run down
 $69FA DEC A         ;
 $69FB JR Z,$6A2C    ; }
 $69FD EX AF,AF'     ;
 $69FE LD A,($9CDE)  ; {Fold the up/down bits out of the direction byte ($9CDE)
 $6A01 LD E,A        ;
 $6A02 AND $0C       ;
 $6A04 JR Z,$6A08    ;
 $6A06 XOR $0C       ; }
*$6A08 RRCA          ; {Combine them with left/right, keep the two step bits
 $6A09 RRCA          ;
 $6A0A OR E          ;
 $6A0B AND $03       ; }
 $6A0D JR Z,$6A13    ; {Any movement: re-arm the timeout
 $6A0F EX AF,AF'     ;
 $6A10 LD A,$64      ;
 $6A12 EX AF,AF'     ; }
*$6A13 LD E,A        ; {Step the letter one place up or down
 $6A14 LD A,C        ;
 $6A15 RR E          ;
 $6A17 ADC A,$00     ;
 $6A19 RR E          ;
 $6A1B SBC A,$00     ; }
 $6A1D CP $5B        ; {Wrap 'Z'+1 round to 'A' and 'A'-1 round to 'Z'
 $6A1F LD C,$41      ;
 $6A21 JR Z,$6A2A    ;
 $6A23 CP $40        ;
 $6A25 LD C,$5A      ;
 $6A27 JR Z,$6A2A    ;
 $6A29 LD C,A        ; }
*$6A2A JR $69E3      ; Redraw and keep editing this letter
*$6A2C LD (HL),C     ; {Store the accepted letter into both the table and the
 $6A2D LD (IY+$00),C ; buffer
 $6A30 INC IY        ;
 $6A32 INC HL        ; }
 $6A33 CALL $6971    ; Wait for input
 $6A36 INC IX        ; {Move on to the next letter
 $6A38 POP BC        ;
 $6A39 DJNZ $69DB    ; }
 $6A3B LD A,$02      ; Start music track 2
 $6A3D CALL $A927    ; Start playing music track A
 $6A40 LD A,$04      ;
 $6A42 LD E,$0E      ;
 $6A44 LD C,$10      ;
 $6A46 CALL $6778    ; Paint attribute colour-wipe column
 $6A49 RET           ;

; Main menu key dispatcher (1P/2P select, redefine keys)
;
; Used by the routine at #R$A94C.
;
; .
;
; Guarded by re-entrancy flag $9C29 (set by #R$A927). Reads keyboard row $F7
; (SPACE/SYM SHIFT/M/N/B) and dispatches by bit: bit 0 -> #R$6A6D (select
; player 1), bit 1 -> #R$6A72 (select player 2), bit 2 -> #R$67C7 (redefine
; keys menu).
@label=menu_dispatch
c$6A4A LD A,($9C29)  ;
 $6A4D AND A         ;
 $6A4E RET NZ        ;
 $6A4F EI            ;
 $6A50 PUSH HL       ;
 $6A51 PUSH DE       ;
 $6A52 PUSH BC       ;
 $6A53 LD A,$F7      ; {read keyboard row $F7
 $6A55 IN A,($FE)    ; }
 $6A57 CPL           ;
 $6A58 RRA           ;
 $6A59 CALL C,$6A6D  ; Print "PLAYER 1"/"PLAYER 2" turn indicator
 $6A5C JR C,$6A68    ;
 $6A5E RRA           ;
 $6A5F CALL C,$6A72  ;
 $6A62 JR C,$6A68    ;
 $6A64 RRA           ;
 $6A65 CALL C,$67C7  ; Redefine keys
*$6A68 POP BC        ;
 $6A69 POP DE        ;
 $6A6A POP HL        ;
 $6A6B DI            ;
 $6A6C RET           ;

; Print "PLAYER 1"/"PLAYER 2" turn indicator
;
; Used by the routine at #R$6A4A.
;
; .
;
; Announces whose turn it is: stores the player number, prints the matching "1
; PLAYER"/"2 PLAYER" message and wipes a colour column beside it.
@label=print_turn_indicator
c$6A6D PUSH AF       ; {entry: set player number to 1
 $6A6E LD A,$01      ;
 $6A70 JR $6A75      ; }
; This entry point is used by the routine at #R$6A4A.
*$6A72 PUSH AF       ; {entry: set player number to 2
 $6A73 LD A,$02      ; }
*$6A75 LD ($9C75),A  ; store player number at $9C75
 $6A78 ADD A,$0E     ; map player number to message $0F/$10 ("1 PLAYER"/"2
                     ; PLAYERS")
 $6A7A CALL $6648    ; Print message N from table $627A
 $6A7D LD A,$0A      ;
 $6A7F LD C,$40      ;
 $6A81 LD E,$13      ;
 $6A83 CALL $6778    ; Paint attribute colour-wipe column
 $6A86 POP AF        ;
 $6A87 RET           ;

; Show credits screen: highlight active player, update HUD, wipe out
;
; Used by the routine at #R$A612.
;
; .
;
; Inits state, prints "PLAYER ONE"/"PLAYER TWO" and draws the credits box
; (#R$6AD4), colours the active player's border white (C=$07, chosen via
; $9C76), updates both players' HUD panels via #R$6771, then transitions out
; with the #R$C6A6 wipe.
@label=show_credits_screen
c$6A88 LD A,$FF      ;
 $6A8A LD ($9C5D),A  ;
 $6A8D LD HL,$9C67   ;
 $6A90 LD ($9C5B),HL ;
 $6A93 DI            ;
 $6A94 CALL $C84C    ; Build wrapped scroll-window row into $F6D1 buffer
 $6A97 CALL $AC8D    ; Object render pass
 $6A9A CALL $C772    ; Fast column mover
 $6A9D EI            ;
 $6A9E HALT          ;
 $6A9F LD A,$03      ; "PLAYER ONE"/"PLAYER TWO" (credits screen)
 $6AA1 CALL $6648    ; Print message N from table $627A
 $6AA4 CALL $6AD4    ; Draw both players' panel borders
 $6AA7 LD A,($9C76)  ; get Active player
 $6AAA LD HL,$58C4   ;
 $6AAD LD DE,$58DA   ;
 $6AB0 DEC A         ;
 $6AB1 JR Z,$6AB4    ;
 $6AB3 EX DE,HL      ;
*$6AB4 LD C,$07      ;
*$6AB6 LD (HL),C     ;
 $6AB7 INC L         ;
 $6AB8 LD (HL),C     ;
 $6AB9 LD A,L        ;
 $6ABA ADD A,$1F     ;
 $6ABC LD L,A        ;
 $6ABD LD (HL),C     ;
 $6ABE INC L         ;
 $6ABF LD (HL),C     ;
 $6AC0 EX DE,HL      ;
 $6AC1 LD A,C        ;
 $6AC2 LD C,$00      ;
 $6AC4 AND A         ;
 $6AC5 JR NZ,$6AB6   ;
 $6AC7 LD A,$01      ;
 $6AC9 CALL $6771    ; Update player's HUD panel
 $6ACC INC A         ;
 $6ACD CALL $6771    ; Update player's HUD panel
 $6AD0 CALL $C6A6    ; Screen wipe transition effect
 $6AD3 RET           ;

; Draw both players' panel borders
;
; Used by the routines at #R$6498 and #R$6A88.
;
; .
;
; Draws a 3-cell border segment for player 1 (bitmap $6CD1 at $59A0, via
; #R$6AF4), two single corner-cap boxes ($58C4/$58DA), then a 3-cell border
; segment for player 2 (bitmap $6CF1 at $5A00).
@label=draw_panel_borders
c$6AD4 LD DE,$6CD1   ;
 $6AD7 LD HL,$59A0   ;
 $6ADA CALL $6AF4    ; Draw a 3-cell border segment
 $6ADD XOR A         ;
 $6ADE LD HL,$58C4   ;
 $6AE1 CALL $6B09    ; Draw bordered box graphic (colour + bitmap) at HL
 $6AE4 XOR A         ;
 $6AE5 LD L,$DA      ;
 $6AE7 CALL $6B09    ; Draw bordered box graphic (colour + bitmap) at HL
 $6AEA LD DE,$6CF1   ;
 $6AED LD HL,$5A00   ;
 $6AF0 CALL $6AF4    ; Draw a 3-cell border segment
 $6AF3 RET           ;

; Draw a 3-cell border segment
;
; Used by the routine at #R$6AD4.
;
; DE bitmap data pointer
; HL attribute base
;
; Draws a border segment as two rows of three box graphics, separated by a
; fixed screen stride.
c$6AF4 LD B,$03      ;
*$6AF6 XOR A         ;
 $6AF7 CALL $6B09    ; Draw bordered box graphic (colour + bitmap) at HL
 $6AFA DJNZ $6AF6    ;
 $6AFC LD A,L        ;
 $6AFD ADD A,$14     ;
 $6AFF LD L,A        ;
 $6B00 LD B,$03      ;
*$6B02 XOR A         ;
 $6B03 CALL $6B09    ; Draw bordered box graphic (colour + bitmap) at HL
 $6B06 DJNZ $6B02    ;
 $6B08 RET           ;

; Draw bordered box graphic (colour + bitmap) at HL
;
; Used by the routines at #R$6AD4, #R$6AF4 and #R$A802.
;
; A attribute colour
; HL attribute-memory address (top-left of the box)
; DE pointer to 32-byte bitmap data (4 columns x 8 rows)
;
; Fills a 2x2 attribute cell block with colour A, converts that attribute
; address to the corresponding pixel address, then copies an 8-byte-tall bitmap
; column from DE into it. Repeats for 4 character columns, alternating between
; the top and bottom row of the block (BIT 0,C) and stepping to the next
; attribute row pair every 2 columns (+$22 to L). Used to draw small bordered
; graphics/tiles (e.g. UI boxes) at a fixed screen position.
@label=draw_box
c$6B09 PUSH BC       ; {save registers
 $6B0A PUSH DE       ;
 $6B0B PUSH HL       ; }
 $6B0C LD (HL),A     ; {fill attribute pair (top row)
 $6B0D INC L         ;
 $6B0E LD (HL),A     ; }
 $6B0F LD BC,$001F   ; {move down one attribute row, fill pair (bottom row)
 $6B12 ADD HL,BC     ;
 $6B13 LD (HL),A     ;
 $6B14 INC L         ;
 $6B15 LD (HL),A     ; }
 $6B16 POP HL        ; {restore original HL, keep a copy
 $6B17 PUSH HL       ; }
 $6B18 LD A,H        ; {convert attribute row to pixel-address row; advance
 $6B19 ADD A,A       ; column
 $6B1A ADD A,A       ;
 $6B1B ADD A,A       ;
 $6B1C AND $7F       ;
 $6B1E LD H,A        ;
 $6B1F INC L         ; }
 $6B20 LD C,$04      ; 4 columns to draw
*$6B22 PUSH HL       ; {save column pointer; 8 pixel rows
 $6B23 LD B,$08      ; }
*$6B25 LD A,(DE)     ; {copy 8 bitmap bytes from DE into this pixel column
 $6B26 INC DE        ;
 $6B27 LD (HL),A     ;
 $6B28 INC H         ;
 $6B29 DJNZ $6B25    ; }
 $6B2B POP HL        ; {restore column pointer, move to previous attribute
 $6B2C DEC L         ; column; exit if done
 $6B2D DEC C         ;
 $6B2E JR Z,$6B3A    ; }
 $6B30 BIT 0,C       ; {continue same character row if column count odd
 $6B32 JR NZ,$6B22   ; }
 $6B34 LD A,L        ; {move to next character row pair, loop
 $6B35 ADD A,$22     ;
 $6B37 LD L,A        ;
 $6B38 JR $6B22      ; }
*$6B3A POP HL        ; {restore registers, advance HL past the box
 $6B3B POP DE        ;
 $6B3C POP BC        ;
 $6B3D INC L         ;
 $6B3E INC L         ; }
 $6B3F RET           ; return

; Tile block 2x2 table (cell -> 2x2 character block)
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Four parallel 256-entry lookup tables (#R$7900/$7A00/$7B00/$7C00). A
; background map cell is a single byte, used as the index into all four tables
; at once; the four bytes read out are the four character codes of a 2x2 tile
; block: #R$7900=top-left, $7A00=top-right, $7B00=bottom-left,
; $7C00=bottom-right. The column decoder #R$C941 reads one cell, writes the top
; pair (#R$7900/$7A00) into buffer row A and the bottom pair ($7B00/$7C00) into
; row B, so each cell renders as a 2-char-wide by 2-char-tall tile block. See

; Initialize IM 2 interrupt vector table and set light ISR
;
; Used by the routine at #R$A5A5.
;
; .
;
; Sets up the interrupt system (IM 2) and starts it pointing at the light
; per-frame handler.
@label=init_im2
c$7D00 DI            ;
 $7D01 LD A,$FE      ; {Set interrupt mode 2, vector table at #R$FE00
 $7D03 LD I,A        ;
 $7D05 IM 2          ; }
 $7D07 LD HL,$FE00   ; {Fill the vector table so every vector reads $FDFD
 $7D0A LD A,$FD      ; }
*$7D0C LD (HL),A     ;
 $7D0D INC L         ;
 $7D0E JR NZ,$7D0C   ;
 $7D10 INC H         ;
 $7D11 LD (HL),A     ;
 $7D12 LD A,$C3      ; {Plant a JP opcode at $FDFD, turning it into a
 $7D14 LD ($FDFD),A  ; trampoline}
 $7D17 LD HL,$A0B0   ; point to per-frame handler #R$A0B0 (light ISR)
 $7D1A LD ($FDFE),HL ; set ISR handler address
 $7D1D EI            ;
 $7D1E RET           ;

; Clear screen and draw title screen graphics
;
; Used by the routine at #R$A5A5.
;
; .
;
; Clears the screen to black, then draws the title-screen logo/artwork.
@label=draw_title_screen
c$7D1F XOR A         ;
 $7D20 OUT ($FE),A   ; Set border colour to black
 $7D22 LD HL,$4000   ; {Clear the bitmap ($4000-$5AFE)
 $7D25 LD DE,$4001   ;
 $7D28 LD (HL),A     ; }
 $7D29 LD BC,$1AFF   ;
 $7D2C LDIR          ;
 $7D2E LD IY,$7D4E   ; IY = attribute data for the graphic blocks (#R$7D4E)
 $7D32 LD HL,$5800   ;
 $7D35 EXX           ;
 $7D36 LD DE,$CB91   ; Left half source data (#R$CB91)
 $7D39 LD HL,$4000   ;
 $7D3C CALL $7D5C    ; Draw title screen graphic block
 $7D3F EXX           ;
 $7D40 LD HL,$5819   ;
 $7D43 EXX           ;
 $7D44 LD DE,$CA09   ; Right half source data (#R$CA09)
 $7D47 LD HL,$4019   ;
 $7D4A CALL $7D5C    ; Draw title screen graphic block
 $7D4D RET           ;

; Title-screen attribute data (IY source for #R$7D5C)
b$7D4E DEFB $06,$06,$06,$06,$47,$47,$45,$42
 $7D56 DEFB $42,$42,$47,$47,$47,$45

; Draw title screen graphic block (attribute rows + bitmap columns)
;
; Used by the routine at #R$7D1F.
;
; IY attribute data pointer
; DE bitmap data pointer
; HL destination screen address
;
; Paints a 7x7 block of coloured character cells onto the screen, using one
; data stream for the colours and another for the pixel shapes.
@label=draw_title_block
c$7D5C LD B,$07      ;
*$7D5E PUSH BC       ;
 $7D5F LD C,$07      ;
 $7D61 LD A,B        ;
 $7D62 CP $03        ; Row 3: shadow-HL needs an extra bitmap-third adjustment
 $7D64 EXX           ;
 $7D65 JR NZ,$7D69   ;
 $7D67 INC H         ; {Bump shadow H for the bitmap-third boundary
 $7D68 INC H         ; }
*$7D69 LD A,(IY+$00) ;
 $7D6C INC IY        ;
 $7D6E LD B,$07      ;
*$7D70 LD (HL),A     ;
 $7D71 INC L         ;
 $7D72 DJNZ $7D70    ; Write attribute byte across 7 columns
 $7D74 LD A,L        ;
 $7D75 ADD A,$19     ; {Advance to next attribute row (+$19)
 $7D77 LD L,A        ; }
 $7D78 EXX           ;
*$7D79 PUSH HL       ;
 $7D7A LD B,$08      ;
*$7D7C LD A,(DE)     ;
 $7D7D LD (HL),A     ;
 $7D7E INC DE        ;
 $7D7F INC H         ;
 $7D80 DJNZ $7D7C    ; Copy 8 bitmap scanlines for this column
 $7D82 POP HL        ;
 $7D83 INC L         ;
 $7D84 DEC C         ;
 $7D85 JR NZ,$7D79   ; Next of 7 columns
 $7D87 LD A,L        ;
 $7D88 ADD A,$19     ;
 $7D8A LD L,A        ;
 $7D8B POP BC        ;
 $7D8C LD A,B        ;
 $7D8D CP $04        ; Row 4: crossing into next screen third
 $7D8F JR NZ,$7D95   ;
 $7D91 LD A,H        ;
 $7D92 ADD A,$10     ; {Bump H to next screen third (+$10)
 $7D94 LD H,A        ; }
*$7D95 DJNZ $7D5E    ; Next of 7 rows
 $7D97 RET           ;

; Decode 9 graphic blocks, then substitute every other byte via table $9A00
;
; Used by the routine at #R$A5A5.
;
; .
;
; Decodes 9 graphic blocks into the #R$CA09 sprite area, then runs a second
; pass to mirror half the decoded bytes.
c$7D98 LD IY,$6B42   ;
 $7D9C LD IX,$F765   ;
 $7DA0 LD HL,$CA09   ;
 $7DA3 LD B,$09      ; 9 block-descriptor entries
*$7DA5 PUSH BC       ;
 $7DA6 CALL $7DC9    ; Decode one graphic-block descriptor entry; HL (the
                     ; output cursor) is shared and left advancing across all 9
                     ; calls
 $7DA9 LD DE,$0011   ;
 $7DAC ADD IY,DE     ; Advance IY to the next 17-byte entry
 $7DAE POP BC        ;
 $7DAF DJNZ $7DA5    ; Loop 9 times
 $7DB1 LD DE,$CA09   ;
 $7DB4 AND A         ;
 $7DB5 SBC HL,DE     ; Total bytes written = HL - #R$CA09
 $7DB7 EX DE,HL      ;
 $7DB8 SRL D         ; {Halve the byte count (process every other byte)
 $7DBA RR E          ; }
 $7DBC LD B,$9A      ;
*$7DBE INC HL        ;
 $7DBF LD C,(HL)     ; {Substitute this byte via table #R$9A00
 $7DC0 LD A,(BC)     ;
 $7DC1 LD (HL),A     ; }
 $7DC2 INC HL        ; Skip the alternate (untouched) byte
 $7DC3 DEC DE        ;
 $7DC4 LD A,D        ;
 $7DC5 OR E          ;
 $7DC6 JR NZ,$7DBE   ; Loop until the halved count reaches zero
 $7DC8 RET           ;

; Decode one graphic-block descriptor entry (IY-indexed)
;
; Used by the routine at #R$7D98.
;
; IY 17-byte block descriptor (called once per entry from #R$7D98's loop)
;
; Decodes one 17-byte block descriptor, expanding its graphic data one or more
; times as the descriptor requests.
c$7DC9 CALL $7DF3    ; Expand one graphic block
 $7DCC LD (IY+$02),L ; {Store the decoded data pointer into the descriptor
 $7DCF LD (IY+$03),H ; (IY+$02/$03)}
 $7DD2 CALL $7E4A    ; Build bit-shifted copies of a graphic block
 $7DD5 LD B,(IY+$0E) ; {Repeat count (IY+$0E); skip the extra loop if zero
 $7DD8 DEC B         ; }
 $7DD9 JR Z,$7DE5    ;
*$7DDB PUSH BC       ;
 $7DDC CALL $7DF3    ; Expand one graphic block
 $7DDF CALL $7E4A    ; Build bit-shifted copies of a graphic block
 $7DE2 POP BC        ;
 $7DE3 DJNZ $7DDB    ;
*$7DE5 SLA (IY+$0A)  ; Shift a flag in the descriptor (IY+$0A)
 $7DE9 LD A,(IY+$06) ; {Bump a counter (IY+$0B) if a flag (IY+$06) is set
 $7DEC AND A         ;
 $7DED JR Z,$7DF2    ; }
 $7DEF INC (IY+$0B)  ;
*$7DF2 RET           ;

; Expand one graphic block (with optional blank-row padding)
;
; Used by the routine at #R$7DC9.
;
; HL destination cursor (in/out, advanced past the written data)
; IX source graphic data pointer (in/out, advanced past the block)
; IY block descriptor
;
; Expands one graphic block into interleaved pixel/mask data at HL, optionally
; padded with blank rows above and below.
c$7DF3 LD A,(IY+$06)  ; IY+$06 selects optional blank-row padding
 $7DF6 AND A          ;
 $7DF7 JR Z,$7E01     ; Skip leading padding if flag clear
 $7DF9 LD B,(IY+$07)  ; Padding row count (IY+$07)
*$7DFC CALL $7E3D     ; Write one blank padding row
 $7DFF DJNZ $7DFC     ; Pad blank rows before the block
*$7E01 PUSH HL        ;
 $7E02 XOR A          ; {Sum per-row column width (IY+$0A x IY+$0B) into A
 $7E03 LD B,(IY+$0B)  ;
*$7E06 ADD A,(IY+$0A) ; }
 $7E09 DJNZ $7E06     ; Sum column width into A (total block width)
 $7E0B LD ($7E1B),A   ; Stash total block width for later
 $7E0E LD C,(IY+$0B)  ; Row count (IY+$0B)
*$7E11 LD B,(IY+$0A)  ; Column count for this row (IY+$0A)
*$7E14 LD A,(IX+$00)  ;
 $7E17 LD (HL),A      ;
 $7E18 INC HL         ;
 $7E19 LD A,(IX+$20)  ; !!MUT-ARG!! patched by $7E0B
 $7E1C LD (HL),A      ;
 $7E1D INC HL         ;
 $7E1E INC IX         ;
 $7E20 DJNZ $7E14     ; Write interleaved byte pair for this column
 $7E22 DEC C          ;
 $7E23 JR NZ,$7E11    ; Next row
 $7E25 LD A,(IY+$06)  ;
 $7E28 AND A          ;
 $7E29 JR Z,$7E33     ; Skip trailing padding if flag clear
 $7E2B LD B,(IY+$07)  ;
*$7E2E CALL $7E3D     ; Write one blank padding row
 $7E31 DJNZ $7E2E     ; Pad blank rows after the block
*$7E33 LD A,($7E1B)   ;
 $7E36 LD E,A         ;
 $7E37 LD D,$00       ;
 $7E39 ADD IX,DE      ; Advance IX by the block's total width
 $7E3B POP HL         ;

; Write one blank padding row (8x $00/$FF byte pairs)
;
; Used by the routine at #R$7DF3.
;
; .
;
; Called from #R$7DF3 to pad a leading/trailing blank row. Writes 8 columns of
; the same interleaved byte-pair layout #R$7DF3 writes for real data (pixel
; byte $00, mask/second-plane byte $FF - i.e. blank pixels, fully transparent).
c$7E3D PUSH BC       ;
 $7E3E LD B,$08      ;
*$7E40 LD (HL),$00   ;
 $7E42 INC HL        ;
 $7E43 LD (HL),$FF   ;
 $7E45 INC HL        ;
 $7E46 DJNZ $7E40    ;
 $7E48 POP BC        ;
 $7E49 RET           ;

; Build bit-shifted copies of a graphic block (smooth-scroll variants)
;
; Used by the routine at #R$7DC9.
;
; HL working cursor (in/out, advanced past the block and its copies)
; IY block descriptor
;
; Makes extra copies of a graphic block, each shifted one bit further right,
; for smooth sub-pixel horizontal scrolling.
c$7E4A LD A,(IY+$06) ;
 $7E4D ADD A,A       ;
 $7E4E JR Z,$7E92    ; Skip shift generation if flag is zero: just advance
                     ; pointer
*$7E50 SRL A         ;
 $7E52 BIT 0,A       ;
 $7E54 JR Z,$7E50    ; Shift-step count = lowest set bit of doubled flag
 $7E56 LD B,A        ;
*$7E57 PUSH BC       ;
 $7E58 LD C,(IY+$0C) ;
 $7E5B LD B,$00      ;
 $7E5D LD E,L        ;
 $7E5E LD D,H        ;
 $7E5F ADD HL,BC     ;
 $7E60 EX DE,HL      ;
 $7E61 LDIR          ; Duplicate block into working copy (offset by IY+$0C)
 $7E63 LD A,$08      ;
 $7E65 SUB (IY+$06)  ;
 $7E68 AND $07       ; Bit-shift amount = (8 - flag) mod 8
 $7E6A LD B,A        ;
*$7E6B PUSH BC       ;
 $7E6C PUSH HL       ;
 $7E6D LD C,(IY+$0A) ;
 $7E70 SLA C         ;
 $7E72 LD B,(IY+$0B) ;
 $7E75 INC B         ;
 $7E76 LD E,C        ;
 $7E77 LD D,$00      ;
*$7E79 PUSH BC       ;
 $7E7A PUSH HL       ;
 $7E7B XOR A         ;
*$7E7C RLA           ;
 $7E7D RR (HL)       ;
 $7E7F RRA           ;
 $7E80 ADD HL,DE     ;
 $7E81 DJNZ $7E7C    ; Shift this column right by 1 bit (carry-propagate)
 $7E83 POP HL        ;
 $7E84 OR (HL)       ;
 $7E85 LD (HL),A     ;
 $7E86 INC HL        ;
 $7E87 POP BC        ;
 $7E88 DEC C         ;
 $7E89 JR NZ,$7E79   ; Next column
 $7E8B POP HL        ;
 $7E8C POP BC        ;
 $7E8D DJNZ $7E6B    ; Next shift amount
 $7E8F POP BC        ;
 $7E90 DJNZ $7E57    ; Next shift step
*$7E92 LD C,(IY+$0C) ;
 $7E95 LD B,$00      ;
 $7E97 ADD HL,BC     ; Advance pointer past this block
 $7E98 RET           ;

; Colour-sequence tail, input state, and the keyboard scan tables
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Holds the end of the animated colour sequence started at $9CCC ($45..$40 then
; the $FF terminator #R$686A wraps on), the input state bytes #R$68B1 writes
; ($9CDC hold count, $9CDD edge flag, $9CDE directions), the five [half-row
; port, key mask] pairs at $9CE0 that #R$68B1 scans for the redefined keys, the
; six half-row port values at $9CEA that #R$6829 scans, immediately before the
; keyboard character map at #R$9CF0.
b$9CD1 DEFB $45,$46,$47,$46,$45,$44,$43,$42
 $9CD9 DEFB $41,$40,$FF
 $9CDC DEFB $00                             ; Input state / action code
 $9CDD DEFB $00,$00,$00,$DF,$01,$BF,$02,$7F
 $9CE5 DEFB $02,$FD,$01,$FD,$02,$FE,$FD,$FB
 $9CED DEFB $DF,$BF,$7F

; Keyboard character map (8 half-rows x 5 keys)
;
; .
;
; .
;
; One entry per key in half-row scan order, indexed by #R$67F1 as $9CF0 + 5*row
; + key: CS,Z,X,C,V then A,S,D,F,G, Q,W,E,R,T, 1,2,3,4,5, 0,9,8,7,6, P,O,I,U,Y,
; ENTER,L,K,J,H and SPACE,SYM SHIFT,M,N,B. Entries hold the key's character,
; except codes $00-$03 which stand in for CAPS SHIFT, SYM SHIFT, SPACE and
; ENTER - #R$67F1 prints those from messages $06-$09 instead of as characters.
b$9CF0 DEFB $00,$5A,$58,$43,$56,$41,$53,$44
 $9CF8 DEFB $46,$47,$51,$57,$45,$52,$54,$31
 $9D00 DEFB $32,$33,$34,$35,$30,$39,$38,$37
 $9D08 DEFB $36,$50,$4F,$49,$55,$59,$03,$4C
 $9D10 DEFB $4B,$4A,$48,$02,$01,$4D,$4E,$42

; Object-group counters (remaining spawn budget per group)
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Four counters #R$B730 seeds to 6/8/4/1 - together exactly the 19 slots in the
; pool at #R$9D40. #R$BA5F spends them when spawning and the handlers give them
; back on retirement, so they cap how many objects of each group can be alive
; at once.
b$9D18 DEFB $00      ; Object-group counter
 $9D19 DEFB $00      ; Object-group counter
 $9D1A DEFB $00      ; Object-group counter
 $9D1B DEFB $00      ; Object-group counter

; Free-object-list head pointer
w$9D1C DEFW $0000    ; Head of the free list chained through each object's +$00
                     ; (see #R$B730)

; Persistent object-list head slots (4 x 6 bytes)
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Four 6-byte records, too small to be objects: they act as list heads and
; sentinels. #R$BDAE walks the object list from $9D1E and #R$B730 pre-sets bits
; 2 and 3 of each record's +$04 flags byte. Each one's +$02 descriptor field
; points at the vector record #R$9D36.
b$9D1E DEFB $00,$00,$3C,$9D,$00,$00 ; Slot 0: the object-list head walked by
                                    ; #R$BDAE
 $9D24 DEFB $00,$00,$3C,$9D,$00,$00 ; Slot 1
 $9D2A DEFB $00,$00,$3C,$9D,$00,$00 ; Slot 2
 $9D30 DEFW $0000                   ; Slot 3: secondary object-stack pointer
 $9D32 DEFB $3C,$9D,$00,$00         ; Slot 3's descriptor pointer and flags

; Vector record the persistent slots point at
;
; .
;
; .
;
; The address every persistent slot's +$02 field holds ($9D3C) lands two words
; into this record, where $9D3C holds #R$AC95 (the render pass's toggle-loop
; head) and $9D3E holds $ACB4 (its SP-restore tail). Nothing in code references
; either address, so they are presumably reached indirectly through this record
; - the dereference has not been traced.
w$9D36 DEFW $9D36
 $9D38 DEFW $9D3E
 $9D3A DEFW $0100
 $9D3C DEFW $AC95
 $9D3E DEFW $ACB4

; Object pool: 19 objects of 29 bytes
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Every actor in the game - the player's plane, enemy planes, tanks, boats,
; cannons, bullets, explosions and bonus items - is one 29-byte ($1D) object
; out of the pool at $9D40, chained through a singly-linked list and dispatched
; through a single state index. Field layout: +$00 next-object pointer; +$02
; descriptor-record pointer (data, not code - see #R$5B55); +$04 status flags
; (bit 0 busy/suppress-redraw, bit 1 alive/retire, bit 2 active, bit 3
; fixed-slot, bit 4 in-transition, bit 5 on-screen, bit 6 mirror, bit 7 facing
; left); +$05 state index, selecting the per-frame handler as jump-table entry
; $29+n (see #R$A000, base $A052); +$06 animation frame; +$07 dx and +$09 dy
; (fixed-point velocity, set by #R$B8A2); +$0B X and +$0D Y (fixed-point
; position, low byte fraction, high byte cell); +$0F respawn/blink timer
; (player); +$10 heading 0-63 ($FF on a projectile = not yet launched); +$11
; speed; +$12 health; +$13 formation-slot id ($FF = none); +$14 collision
; hit-mask (see #R$BCE9); +$15/+$16 reused per object type - movement-script
; pointer for script-driven enemies (#R$B94E), bank-delay timer plus current
; bank frame for the player (#R$BE4A), the group-counter address for an
; explosion (#R$C5AF), the direction-rate for the weave handler (#R$C3C7); +$17
; script byte cache / player bank target; +$18 script frame-delay timer or
; player invulnerability countdown; +$19 script loop counter; +$1A target
; reference ($FF = none) or stage counter; +$1B from spawn-template byte 3 plus
; difficulty, purpose unconfirmed; +$1C heading steered toward the target by
; #R$C43C (distinct from +$10). Because +$15/+$16, +$17 and +$18 all mean
; different things depending on +$05, a port must key their meaning off the
; state index rather than assuming one role per byte. See docs/Actors.md.
b$9D40 DEFB $00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00 ; {19
 $9D5D DEFB $00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00 ; objects of
 $9D7A DEFB $00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00 ; 29 bytes
 $9D97 DEFB $00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00 ; ($9D40-$9F66),
 $9DB4 DEFB $00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00 ; chained
 $9DD1 DEFB $00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00 ; into the
 $9DEE DEFB $00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00 ; free list
 $9E0B DEFB $00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00 ; by #R$B730
 $9E28 DEFB $00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00 ;

; Object state/animation jump-table (used with $B7F6, various offsets)
;
; .
;
; .
;
; One continuous 73-entry word table of code addresses, live-verified: every
; entry (#R$A000-$A091) points into valid code (#R$A445-#R$C3C7 range).
; Different routines index into different sub-ranges of this same table via
; #R$B7F6 (e.g. $A02A, $A02E, $A038, $A042, $A052, $A076 are all just offsets
; into it, not separate tables). Ends at #R$A092, immediately followed by the
; score-value table at $A094 (see #R$66B5).
w$A000 DEFW $AFC3    ; $00 - Update tile-block tables
 $A002 DEFW $B121    ; $01 - Masked blit setup (to tile-block table)
 $A004 DEFW $B005    ; $02 - Opaque tile blit
 $A006 DEFW $B12B    ; $03 - Masked tile blit setup
 $A008 DEFW $B072    ; $04 - Update tile-block tables
 $A00A DEFW $B13F    ; $05 - Masked blit setup (to tile-block table)
 $A00C DEFW $B0B4    ; $06 - Opaque tile blit
 $A00E DEFW $B14A    ; $07 - Masked blit setup
 $A010 DEFW $B3FE    ; $08 - Draw masked sprite 8-row mask-rev
 $A012 DEFW $B1BE    ; $09 - Draw masked sprite 16-row mask-rev
 $A014 DEFW $B452    ; $0A - Draw masked sprite 8-row pixel-rev
 $A016 DEFW $B24A    ; $0B - Draw masked sprite 16-row pixel-rev
 $A018 DEFW $B4AA    ; $0C - Draw masked sprite 8-row mask-rev
 $A01A DEFW $B2DA    ; $0D - Draw masked sprite 16-row mask-rev
 $A01C DEFW $B502    ; $0E - Draw masked sprite 8-row pixel-rev
 $A01E DEFW $B36A    ; $0F - Draw masked sprite 16-row pixel-rev
 $A020 DEFW $B15B    ; $10 - OR-composite tile-block pages onto screen
 $A022 DEFW $B55E    ; $11 - Copy 8-wide screen strips
 $A024 DEFW $B61A    ; $12 - Copy 8-wide screen strips (transparent)
 $A026 DEFW $B72D    ; $13 - => Formation script
 $A028 DEFW $AFC1    ; $14 - Jump to (IX)
 $A02A DEFW $A445    ; $15 - Draw scrolling scenery column using tile generator
 $A02C DEFW $A46C    ; $16 - Draw scrolling scenery column
 $A02E DEFW $A894    ; $17 - Start game
 $A030 DEFW $A894    ; $18 - Start game
 $A032 DEFW $A894    ; $19 - Start game
 $A034 DEFW $A802    ; $1A - Show bonus-points award screen, transition onward
 $A036 DEFW $A783    ; $1B - Player death-check entry
 $A038 DEFW $A588    ; $1C - No-op
 $A03A DEFW $A894    ; $1D - Start game
 $A03C DEFW $A8A7    ; $1E
 $A03E DEFW $A589    ; $1F - Exit gameplay
 $A040 DEFW $A589    ; $20 - Exit gameplay
 $A042 DEFW $A15E    ; $21 - No-op
 $A044 DEFW $A15E    ; $22 - No-op
 $A046 DEFW $A15E    ; $23 - No-op
 $A048 DEFW $A15E    ; $24 - No-op
 $A04A DEFW $A1AF    ; $25 - Restrict event mask to bit 7, run scenery script
 $A04C DEFW $A15F    ; $26 - Redraw HUD (deferred)
 $A04E DEFW $A178    ; $27 - Redraw score, check bonus life (deferred)
 $A050 DEFW $A16D    ; $28 - Load pending sound effect (deferred)
 $A052 DEFW $BE02    ; $29 - No-op
 $A054 DEFW $BE01    ; $2A - Player frozen
 $A056 DEFW $BE03    ; $2B - Player
 $A058 DEFW $BFEB    ; $2C - Check for bullet hit, start explosion
 $A05A DEFW $C051    ; $2D - Move straight down at fixed speed; advance
                     ; animation frame
 $A05C DEFW $C075    ; $2E - Multi-hit enemy
 $A05E DEFW $C075    ; $2F - Multi-hit enemy
 $A060 DEFW $C3C7    ; $30 - Movement handler $30
 $A062 DEFW $C31A    ; $31 - Movement handler $31
 $A064 DEFW $C199    ; $32 - Multi-hit enemy
 $A066 DEFW $C199    ; $33 - Multi-hit enemy
 $A068 DEFW $C298    ; $34 - Movement handler $34
 $A06A DEFW $C11C    ; $35 - Scripted-movement enemy
 $A06C DEFW $C015    ; $36 - Launch and move projectile; explode on hit
 $A06E DEFW $C217    ; $37 - Movement handler $37
 $A070 DEFW $C388    ; $38 - Movement handler $38
 $A072 DEFW $C359    ; $39 - Movement handler $39
 $A074 DEFW $C199    ; $3A - Multi-hit enemy
; Movement script opcodes (see #R$B8F9)
 $A076 DEFW $B941    ; $3B - mvop $00 dispatch sub-command (C bits 3-6) via
                     ; $A082
 $A078 DEFW $B95F    ; $3C - mvop $01 set field IY+$19 (from C or next script
                     ; byte)
 $A07A DEFW $B974    ; $3D - mvop $02 set absolute heading, apply velocity
 $A07C DEFW $B992    ; $3E - mvop $03 turn heading relative, apply velocity
 $A07E DEFW $B9BC    ; $3F - mvop $04 set/clear mirror flag (IY+$04 bit 6)
 $A080 DEFW $B9CA    ; $40 - mvop $05 set N object fields from script
                     ; (offset,value pairs)
 $A082 DEFW $B9E3    ; $41 - clear velocity (dx,dy = 0)
 $A084 DEFW $B9F1    ; $42 - loop back in script until counter IY+$19 expires
 $A086 DEFW $BA0A    ; $43 - Apply object velocity
 $A088 DEFW $BA23    ; $44 - no-op
 $A08A DEFW $BA25    ; $45 - set object alive flag (IY+$04 bit 1)
 $A08C DEFW $BA2B    ; $46 - turn heading toward target ($9C6D)
 $A08E DEFW $BA43    ; $47 - set random column (IY+$0C)
 $A090 DEFW $BA4F    ; $48 - randomly set/clear direction flag (IY+$04 bit 7)

; Jump-table terminator, then the score-value table at $A094 (3 bytes/entry,
; see #R$66B5)
b$A092 DEFB $00,$00,$10,$00,$02,$00,$00,$01

; Interrupt handler (light): bump frame counter, set vblank flag
;
; Used by the routine at #R$FDFD.
;
; .
;
; Live-traced: this is the active per-frame handler right after pressing "1" to
; start. Which game phase uses this vs #R$A0C4 is not yet confirmed.
@label=isr_light
c$A0B0 PUSH AF       ;
 $A0B1 PUSH HL       ;
 $A0B2 LD HL,$9BA2   ; {Set vblank flag ($9BA2 bit 7)
 $A0B5 SET 7,(HL)    ; }
 $A0B7 LD HL,$9BA0   ; {Bump frame counter ($9BA0)
 $A0BA INC (HL)      ; }
 $A0BB LD HL,$A1BB   ; {Reset $A1BB to $7F
 $A0BE LD (HL),$7F   ; }
 $A0C0 POP HL        ;
 $A0C1 POP AF        ;
 $A0C2 EI            ;
 $A0C3 RET           ;

; Interrupt handler (heavy): saves shadow regs, dispatches
; enemy/player/collision/sprite updates
;
; .
;
; .
;
; The main per-frame handler: saves all registers, updates the frame counter
; and a couple of pseudo-random values, burns some fixed time, then runs the
; frame's game logic before restoring everything and returning.
@label=isr_heavy
c$A0C4 PUSH AF       ; {Save all registers (both banks)
 $A0C5 PUSH HL       ;
 $A0C6 PUSH DE       ;
 $A0C7 PUSH BC       ;
 $A0C8 EX AF,AF'     ;
 $A0C9 EXX           ;
 $A0CA PUSH AF       ;
 $A0CB PUSH HL       ;
 $A0CC PUSH DE       ;
 $A0CD PUSH BC       ;
 $A0CE PUSH IX       ;
 $A0D0 PUSH IY       ; }
 $A0D2 LD HL,$9BA2   ; {Set vblank flag ($9BA2 bit 7)
 $A0D5 SET 7,(HL)    ; }
 $A0D7 LD HL,$9BA0   ; {Bump frame counter and rotate a byte ($9BA0/$9BA1)
 $A0DA INC (HL)      ;
 $A0DB INC HL        ; }
 $A0DC RLC (HL)      ;
 $A0DE LD HL,$A1BB   ; {Reset $A1BB to $7F
 $A0E1 LD (HL),$7F   ; }
 $A0E3 LD HL,($9C35) ; {Advance pseudo-random shift value ($9C35/$9C34)
 $A0E6 ADD HL,HL     ;
 $A0E7 LD ($9C35),HL ;
 $A0EA SBC A,A       ;
 $A0EB LD ($9C34),A  ; }
 $A0EE LD HL,($9C39) ; {Advance another pseudo-random shift value ($9C39/$9C38)
 $A0F1 ADD HL,HL     ;
 $A0F2 LD ($9C39),HL ;
 $A0F5 SBC A,A       ;
 $A0F6 LD ($9C38),A  ; }
 $A0F9 LD A,$08      ; {Burn fixed time in a delay loop
*$A0FB LD B,$0F      ;
*$A0FD DJNZ $A0FD    ;
 $A0FF AND $FF       ;
 $A101 INC HL        ;
 $A102 DEC A         ; }
 $A103 JP NZ,$A0FB   ;
 $A106 CALL $C72A    ; Animate active player's indicator box colour
 $A109 CALL $BBE5    ; Mark active objects into the attribute-buffer collision
                     ; mask
 $A10C CALL $BCE9    ; Draw active objects' collision masks into attribute
                     ; buffer
 $A10F CALL $BBC2    ; Clear buffers at $7F00-$7FFF and $8000-$80FF
 $A112 CALL $C772    ; Fast column mover
 $A115 CALL $C680    ; Scroll background
 $A118 CALL $C8B8    ; Advance background scroll
 $A11B CALL $C84C    ; Build wrapped scroll-window row into $F6D1 buffer
 $A11E CALL $C9AF    ; Advance enemy timeline
 $A121 CALL $BD99    ; Update randomized countdown, then enter player update
 $A124 CALL $AC8D    ; Object render pass
 $A127 CALL $A561    ; Player respawn/continue state check
 $A12A POP IY        ;
 $A12C POP IX        ;
 $A12E POP BC        ;
 $A12F POP DE        ;
 $A130 POP HL        ;
 $A131 POP AF        ;
 $A132 EXX           ;
 $A133 EX AF,AF'     ;
 $A134 POP BC        ;
 $A135 POP DE        ;
 $A136 POP HL        ;
 $A137 POP AF        ;
 $A138 EI            ;
 $A139 RET           ;

; Dispatch highest-priority pending deferred event
;
; Used by the routines at #R$A255 and #R$A8C0.
;
; .
;
; Picks the highest-priority pending deferred event (bits set by #R$66B5,
; $A1EA, $A8CF/$BF57/$C33B/$C373, $C8C9) and dispatches its handler.
@label=dispatch_deferred_event
c$A13A LD HL,$9C28   ; {Pending events ($9C27) ANDed with enable/priority mask
 $A13D LD A,($9C27)  ; ($9C28)}
 $A140 AND (HL)      ; {Exit if no enabled event pending
 $A141 RET Z         ; }
 $A142 LD B,(HL)     ; {Save current enable mask
 $A143 PUSH BC       ; }
 $A144 LD B,$FF      ;
 $A146 LD C,A        ;
 $A147 LD A,B        ;
*$A148 INC B         ; {Find lowest set bit (highest priority)
 $A149 RRA           ;
 $A14A CP C          ;
 $A14B JR NC,$A148   ; }
 $A14D AND C         ; {Clear the chosen bit from $9C27
 $A14E LD ($9C27),A  ; }
 $A151 LD A,B        ; {B = bit index -> jump-table selector
 $A152 LD HL,$A042   ; }
 $A155 CALL $B7F6    ; Jump-table dispatcher
 $A158 POP AF        ;
 $A159 LD ($9C28),A  ; Restore the enable mask
 $A15C SCF           ;
 $A15D RET           ;

; No-op
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Handler for indices $21, $22, $23, $24 of the #R$A000 jump table (see
; #R$B7F6).
@label=noop_A15E
c$A15E RET           ;

; Deferred event $26: mask event bits, redraw active player's HUD
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Restricts the event-enable mask $9C28 to bit 7 only, then redraws the active
; player's HUD panel (#R$6771).
c$A15F LD HL,$9C28   ;
 $A162 LD A,$80      ;
 $A164 AND (HL)      ;
 $A165 LD (HL),A     ;
 $A166 LD A,($9C76)  ; get Active player
 $A169 CALL $6771    ; Update player's HUD panel
 $A16C RET           ;

; Deferred event $28: clear event bit 0, load pending sound effect
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Clears bit 0 of the event-enable mask $9C28, then loads the pending sound
; effect via #R$A1F2.
c$A16D LD HL,$9C28   ;
 $A170 LD A,$FE      ;
 $A172 AND (HL)      ;
 $A173 LD (HL),A     ;
 $A174 CALL $A1F2    ; Load parameters for the pending sound effect
 $A177 RET           ;

; Deferred event $27: mask event bits, redraw score and check bonus life
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Restricts the event-enable mask $9C28 to bit 7 only, then reprints the active
; player's score (#R$66DE) and awards a bonus life if the threshold was crossed
; (#R$A189).
c$A178 LD HL,$9C28   ;
 $A17B LD A,$80      ;
 $A17D AND (HL)      ;
 $A17E LD (HL),A     ;
 $A17F LD A,($9C76)  ; get Active player
 $A182 CALL $66DE    ; Print a player's score at its HUD position
 $A185 CALL $A189    ; Award bonus life when score threshold reached
 $A188 RET           ;

; Award bonus life when score threshold reached
;
; Used by the routines at #R$A178 and #R$A802.
;
; IX active player's data block
;
; Checks a player's score against the next bonus-life threshold, and if
; crossed, grants an extra life (up to a cap) and redraws the lives/bombs
; icons.
@label=award_bonus_life
c$A189 LD IX,($9C77) ; Threshold index (IX+$04)
 $A18D LD E,(IX+$04) ;
 $A190 LD D,$00      ;
 $A192 LD HL,$9CB8   ; {Compare score (IX+$00) against threshold table $9CB8
 $A195 ADD HL,DE     ;
 $A196 LD A,(IX+$00) ; }
 $A199 CP (HL)       ;
 $A19A RET C         ;
 $A19B INC (IX+$04)  ; Advance threshold index
 $A19E LD A,(IX+$03) ; {Cap lives at 10 (IX+$03), else grant one more life
 $A1A1 CP $0A        ;
 $A1A3 RET Z         ;
 $A1A4 INC A         ; }
 $A1A5 LD (IX+$03),A ;
 $A1A8 LD A,($9C76)  ; get Active player
 $A1AB CALL $672C    ; Draw lives/bombs icon rows for a player
 $A1AE RET           ;

; Restrict event mask to bit 7, run scenery script
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Handler for index $25 of the #R$A000 jump table (see #R$B7F6).
; .
; Restricts which deferred events can interrupt to only the highest-priority
; class, then runs the scenery/event script interpreter.
c$A1AF LD HL,$9C28   ; {Mask event-enable mask ($9C28) down to bit 7 only
 $A1B2 LD A,$80      ;
 $A1B4 AND (HL)      ;
 $A1B5 LD (HL),A     ; }
 $A1B6 CALL $A3A0    ; Scenery/event script interpreter
 $A1B9 RET           ;

; Sound-effect state: pending priority ($A1BA), segment marker ($A1BB),
; parameter working buffer ($A1BC)
b$A1BA DEFB $00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00
 $A1C2 DEFB $00,$00,$00,$00,$00,$00

; Clear pending sound-effect priority
;
; Used by the routine at #R$A8C0.
;
; .
;
; Clears the pending sound-effect priority, silencing any request that has not
; been picked up yet.
@label=sfx_clear
c$A1C8 LD HL,$A1BA   ;
 $A1CB LD (HL),$00   ;
 $A1CD RET           ;

; Request sound effect at maximum priority
;
; Used by the routines at #R$A589 and #R$A8A7.
;
; .
;
; Requests a sound effect at the highest priority, so it always displaces
; whatever is pending.
@label=sfx_req_max
c$A1CE LD A,$F0      ;
 $A1D0 CALL $A1D4    ; Request sound effect if higher priority than current
 $A1D3 RET           ;

; Request sound effect if higher priority than current
;
; Used by the routines at #R$A1CE and #R$BF42.
;
; A effect priority (high nibble)
;
; Compares the high nibble of A against the currently pending effect's priority
; (stored at (#R$A1BA)); if A's priority is >= the current one, updates it,
; marks ($A1BB)=$80, and sets bit 0 of $9C27 to request dispatch via
; #R$A13A/#R$A222.
@label=sfx_request
c$A1D4 PUSH HL       ;
 $A1D5 PUSH BC       ;
 $A1D6 LD HL,$A1BA   ;
 $A1D9 LD C,A        ;
 $A1DA LD A,(HL)     ;
 $A1DB AND $F0       ; {Mask current pending priority (high nibble)
 $A1DD LD B,A        ; }
 $A1DE LD A,C        ;
 $A1DF AND $F0       ; Mask new request's priority (high nibble)
 $A1E1 CP B          ;
 $A1E2 JR C,$A1EF    ; Skip if new priority is lower
 $A1E4 LD (HL),C     ; Store new priority as pending
 $A1E5 LD A,$80      ; {Mark ready flag $A1BB=$80
 $A1E7 LD ($A1BB),A  ; }
 $A1EA LD HL,$9C27   ; {Request dispatch via $9C27 bit 0
 $A1ED SET 0,(HL)    ; }
*$A1EF POP BC        ;
 $A1F0 POP HL        ;
 $A1F1 RET           ;

; Load parameters for the pending sound effect
;
; Used by the routines at #R$A16D and #R$A255.
;
; .
;
; Loads the parameters for the currently-pending sound effect from a table into
; a working buffer, ready for #R$A222 to play it.
@label=sfx_load_params
c$A1F2 LD A,($A1BA)  ;
 $A1F5 AND $0F       ; {Check priority nibble; jump to idle if zero
 $A1F7 JP Z,$A324    ; }
 $A1FA DEC A         ; {(priority-1)*8 -> byte offset into #R$A329 table
 $A1FB RLCA          ;
 $A1FC RLCA          ;
 $A1FD RLCA          ; }
 $A1FE LD E,A        ;
 $A1FF LD D,$00      ;
 $A201 LD HL,$A329   ; {Point HL at this priority's 8-byte parameter entry
 $A204 ADD HL,DE     ; }
 $A205 LD DE,$A1BC   ;
 $A208 LD BC,$0007   ; {Copy first 7 bytes into working buffer $A1BC
 $A20B LDIR          ; }
 $A20D LD A,(HL)     ; {Low nibble of 8th byte -> extra field
 $A20E AND $0F       ;
 $A210 LD (DE),A     ; }
 $A211 INC DE        ;
 $A212 XOR (HL)      ; {Combine+rotate for second extra field (high nibble)
 $A213 RRCA          ;
 $A214 RRCA          ;
 $A215 RRCA          ;
 $A216 RRCA          ;
 $A217 LD (DE),A     ; }
 $A218 LD HL,$A1C2   ; {C = last copied parameter byte
 $A21B LD C,(HL)     ; }
 $A21C LD HL,$A1C5   ; {HL -> tone-length source; A = first parameter byte
 $A21F LD A,($A1BC)  ; }

; Play sound effect (timed speaker-bit toggle)
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Plays the loaded sound effect as a square-wave tone by toggling the speaker
; bit in a timed delay loop, the same technique used by the music engine.
@label=sfx_play_tone
c$A222 LD (HL),A     ; {Store two more parameter bytes into the working buffer
 $A223 INC HL        ;
 $A224 LD A,($A1BE)  ;
 $A227 LD (HL),A     ; }
 $A228 LD A,($A1C3)  ; {Copy $A1C3 into $A1C7 (setup source pointer)
 $A22B LD ($A1C7),A  ; }
 $A22E BIT 7,C       ; Select tone-length source via C bit 7
 $A230 EXX           ;
 $A231 LD HL,$A1C5   ;
 $A234 LD E,L        ;
 $A235 LD D,H        ;
 $A236 JR Z,$A23B    ; Pick $A1C5 vs $A1C6 pointer variant
 $A238 LD DE,$A1C6   ;
*$A23B EXX           ;
 $A23C LD B,$01      ;
; This entry point is used by the routines at #R$A255 and #R$A31D.
*$A23E EXX           ;
 $A23F LD C,$02      ;
 $A241 LD A,$18      ; A=$18: toggle-on value (border+speaker bit)
*$A243 LD B,(HL)     ;
 $A244 OUT ($FE),A   ; Write toggle value to port $FE
*$A246 NOP           ;
 $A247 NOP           ;
 $A248 NOP           ;
 $A249 DJNZ $A246    ; Hold half-cycle for B ticks (NOP-counted delay)
 $A24B EX DE,HL      ; Swap duration-source pointer for next half-cycle
 $A24C LD A,$00      ;
 $A24E DEC C         ; {Loop 2 half-cycles (one full square-wave period)
 $A24F JR NZ,$A243   ; }
 $A251 EXX           ;
 $A252 LD A,($A1BB)  ;

; Between-segment handler for the sound-effect player
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Called between tone segments of #R$A222's player when $A1BB
; (segment-remaining counter) is nonzero. Dispatches other pending deferred
; events via #R$A13A (same "poll between beats" pattern as the music engine's
; #R$A94C), then checks a completion marker: if it equals $80, reloads a new
; pending sound effect via #R$A1F2; otherwise continues the current effect's
; tone loop.
@label=sfx_next_segment
c$A255 AND A         ;
 $A256 JR Z,$A23E    ; If no segments remain, resume tone loop (#R$A23E)
 $A258 PUSH BC       ;
 $A259 EXX           ;
 $A25A PUSH HL       ;
 $A25B PUSH DE       ;
 $A25C CALL $A13A    ; Dispatch highest-priority pending deferred event
 $A25F POP DE        ;
 $A260 POP HL        ;
 $A261 EXX           ;
 $A262 POP BC        ;
 $A263 LD HL,$A1BB   ; {Read and clear completion marker $A1BB
 $A266 LD A,(HL)     ;
 $A267 LD (HL),$00   ; }
 $A269 CP $80        ; {Marker $80: effect done, load next effect (#R$A1F2)
 $A26B JR Z,$A1F2    ; }
 $A26D BIT 7,C       ; Mode bit (C bit 7) selects which delta pair to apply
 $A26F JR Z,$A281    ;
 $A271 LD HL,$A1C5   ;
 $A274 LD A,($A1BD)  ;
 $A277 ADD A,(HL)    ;
 $A278 LD (HL),A     ;
 $A279 INC HL        ;
 $A27A LD A,($A1BF)  ;
 $A27D ADD A,(HL)    ;
 $A27E LD (HL),A     ;
 $A27F JR $A293      ;
*$A281 LD HL,$A1C5   ;
 $A284 LD A,($A1BD)  ;
 $A287 BIT 0,B       ;
 $A289 JR NZ,$A291   ;
 $A28B LD HL,$A1C6   ;
 $A28E LD A,($A1BF)  ;
*$A291 ADD A,(HL)    ;
 $A292 LD (HL),A     ;
*$A293 LD HL,$A1C7   ; {Decrement segment counter; resume tone loop if more
 $A296 DEC (HL)      ; remain
 $A297 JR NZ,$A23E   ; }
 $A299 LD HL,$A1C1   ;
 $A29C DEC (HL)      ; {Decrement repeat count; idle (#R$A324) when it hits
 $A29D JP Z,$A324    ; zero}
 $A2A0 LD HL,$A1C0   ;
 $A2A3 LD E,(HL)     ;
 $A2A4 LD HL,$A1BD   ;
 $A2A7 LD A,(HL)     ;
 $A2A8 ADD A,E       ;
 $A2A9 LD (HL),A     ;
 $A2AA LD HL,$A1BF   ;
 $A2AD LD A,(HL)     ;
 $A2AE ADD A,E       ;
 $A2AF LD (HL),A     ;
 $A2B0 BIT 5,C       ; C bit 5: toggle the $A1C3 sub-counter
 $A2B2 JR Z,$A2BC    ;
 $A2B4 LD HL,$A1C3   ;
 $A2B7 DEC (HL)      ;
 $A2B8 JR NZ,$A2BC   ;
 $A2BA LD (HL),$01   ;
*$A2BC BIT 3,C       ; C bit 3: negate pitch delta ($A1BD) - sweep reversal
 $A2BE JR Z,$A2CF    ;
 $A2C0 BIT 7,C       ;
 $A2C2 JR NZ,$A2C8   ;
 $A2C4 BIT 0,B       ;
 $A2C6 JR Z,$A2CF    ;
*$A2C8 LD HL,$A1BD   ;
 $A2CB LD A,(HL)     ;
 $A2CC NEG           ;
 $A2CE LD (HL),A     ;
*$A2CF BIT 4,C       ; C bit 4: negate duration delta ($A1BF) - sweep reversal
 $A2D1 JR Z,$A2E2    ;
 $A2D3 BIT 7,C       ;
 $A2D5 JR NZ,$A2DB   ;
 $A2D7 BIT 0,B       ;
 $A2D9 JR NZ,$A2E2   ;
*$A2DB LD HL,$A1BF   ;
 $A2DE LD A,(HL)     ;
 $A2DF NEG           ;
 $A2E1 LD (HL),A     ;
*$A2E2 BIT 6,C       ; C bit 6: reload base pitch/duration from $A1BC/$A1BE
 $A2E4 JR Z,$A2F2    ;
 $A2E6 LD HL,$A1C5   ;
 $A2E9 LD A,($A1BC)  ;
 $A2EC LD (HL),A     ;
 $A2ED INC HL        ;
 $A2EE LD A,($A1BE)  ;
 $A2F1 LD (HL),A     ;
*$A2F2 EXX           ;
 $A2F3 LD HL,$A1C5   ;
 $A2F6 LD DE,$A1C6   ;
 $A2F9 LD A,($A1C3)  ;
 $A2FC EXX           ;
 $A2FD BIT 7,C       ;
 $A2FF JR NZ,$A31E   ;
 $A301 LD A,($A1C1)  ;
 $A304 LD B,C        ;
 $A305 SRL A         ;
 $A307 JR NC,$A30F   ;
 $A309 JR NZ,$A30D   ;
 $A30B RR B          ;
*$A30D RR B          ;
*$A30F BIT 0,B       ;
 $A311 EXX           ;
 $A312 LD A,($A1C3)  ;
 $A315 JR NZ,$A31B   ;
 $A317 EX DE,HL      ;
 $A318 LD A,($A1C4)  ;
*$A31B LD E,L        ;
 $A31C LD D,H        ;

; Sound-effect helper entry points, ending in priority-clear idle path
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Two shared tail entry points for the sound-effect player: one resumes the
; tone loop, the other clears the pending effect to idle.
c$A31D EXX           ;
; This entry point is used by the routine at #R$A255.
*$A31E LD ($A1C7),A  ; Store A, resume #R$A222's tone loop
 $A321 JP $A23E      ;
; This entry point is used by the routines at #R$A1F2 and #R$A255.
*$A324 XOR A         ; {Clear pending sound-effect priority (idle)
 $A325 LD ($A1BA),A  ; }
 $A328 RET           ;

 $A359 DEFB $A0,$F8,$70,$FE,$FC,$0D,$45,$44
 $A361 DEFB $70,$08,$50,$FA,$00,$05,$14,$13
 $A369 DEFB $70,$08,$50,$FA,$00,$08,$15,$13

; Scenery/event script interpreter (wait or dispatch event)
;
; Used by the routines at #R$A1AF, #R$A4E7 and #R$A8C0.
;
; .
;
; Steps the background scenery/event script one instruction at a time. It takes
; nothing in registers - the script pointer is $9BFD and $9BFF gates whether
; the script runs at all. Each script byte is either a wait delay, a
; loop-back-to-start marker, or an event to dispatch; once a wait or event has
; been actioned, this also renders the sub-pixel scrolled scenery graphic.
; Distinct from the enemy-formation (#R$AFB8) and object-movement (#R$B8F9)
; script systems.
@label=scenery_script
c$A3A0 LD A,($9BFF)  ; {Bail out if the script isn't currently active
 $A3A3 CP $FF        ;
 $A3A5 JR NZ,$A3E2   ; }
*$A3A7 LD HL,($9BFD) ; {Read next script byte; if not top-bit-set, handle
 $A3AA LD A,(HL)     ; wait/loop below
 $A3AB AND A         ;
 $A3AC JP P,$A3C6    ; }
 $A3AF CP $FF        ; {$FF: loop-back marker
 $A3B1 JR Z,$A3BE    ; }
 $A3B3 AND $0F       ; {Otherwise: wait delay = byte's low nibble
 $A3B5 LD ($9BAF),A  ; }
 $A3B8 INC HL        ; {Advance pointer past a wait byte, loop
 $A3B9 LD ($9BFD),HL ;
 $A3BC JR $A3A7      ; }
*$A3BE LD HL,($9BFB) ; {Rewind script pointer to default, loop
 $A3C1 LD ($9BFD),HL ;
 $A3C4 JR $A3A7      ; }
*$A3C6 LD HL,$6E06   ; {Top bit set: sum offset-chain table $6E06 to find event
 $A3C9 AND A         ; target
 $A3CA JR Z,$A3D3    ;
 $A3CC LD B,A        ;
 $A3CD LD D,$00      ;
*$A3CF LD E,(HL)     ;
 $A3D0 ADD HL,DE     ;
 $A3D1 DJNZ $A3CF    ; }
*$A3D3 INC HL        ; {Store event pointer, reset its parameter-nibble parity
 $A3D4 LD ($9C0C),HL ;
 $A3D7 LD A,$F0      ;
 $A3D9 LD ($9C0E),A  ; }
 $A3DC CALL $A4C4    ; Extract next 4-bit parameter from scenery-event data
 $A3DF LD ($9BFF),A  ;
*$A3E2 LD HL,$9BAD   ; {Advance the wait/shift timer; return early while still
 $A3E5 NEG           ; counting
 $A3E7 ADD A,(HL)    ;
 $A3E8 RET NC        ; }
 $A3E9 LD (HL),A     ; {Reset a per-event byte counter
 $A3EA XOR A         ;
 $A3EB LD ($9C0A),A  ; }
 $A3EE CALL $A4C4    ; Extract next 4-bit parameter from scenery-event data
 $A3F1 LD HL,$A02A   ; Point to jump table
 $A3F4 CALL $B7F6    ; Jump-table dispatcher
 $A3F7 CALL $A40B    ; Render sub-pixel scrolled graphic
 $A3FA LD HL,($9BFD) ; {Advance past the consumed script byte
 $A3FD INC HL        ;
 $A3FE LD ($9BFD),HL ; }
 $A401 XOR A         ; {Reset wait timer and mark script active again
 $A402 LD ($9BAF),A  ;
 $A405 LD A,$FF      ;
 $A407 LD ($9BFF),A  ; }
 $A40A RET           ;

; Render sub-pixel scrolled graphic (shift amount from scenery script)
;
; Used by the routine at #R$A3A0.
;
; .
;
; Renders the scenery graphic shifted by the scenery-script's wait value, for
; smooth sub-pixel horizontal scrolling.
c$A40B LD A,($9BAF)  ;
 $A40E AND A         ;
 $A40F JR Z,$A441    ; Skip render if wait value is zero
 $A411 NEG           ;
 $A413 ADD A,$08     ; Displacement = 8 - wait value
 $A415 LD ($A436),A  ; Self-modify the shifted-read operand at $A436
 $A418 LD A,($9BFF)  ; {C = pass count
 $A41B LD C,A        ; }
 $A41C LD HL,($9BAB) ; get Scenery data pointer
 $A41F LD IX,$9BE6   ;
*$A423 LD B,$09      ; Outer: 9-byte copy loop setup
*$A425 LD A,(HL)     ;
 $A426 INC L         ;
 $A427 LD (IX+$00),A ; {Duplicate byte into both halves of the double buffer
 $A42A LD (IX+$09),A ; (wrap-safe shift)
 $A42D INC IX        ; }
 $A42F DJNZ $A425    ;
 $A431 LD E,L        ;
 $A432 LD B,$09      ;
*$A434 LD A,(IX+$00) ; !!MUT-ARG!! Read back from the self-modified shifted
                     ; offset (patched by $A415)
 $A437 DEC IX        ;
 $A439 DEC L         ;
 $A43A LD (HL),A     ; Write shifted byte, walking backward
 $A43B DJNZ $A434    ;
 $A43D LD L,E        ;
 $A43E DEC C         ;
 $A43F JR NZ,$A423   ; Repeat for C passes
*$A441 LD ($9BAB),HL ; set Scenery data pointer
 $A444 RET           ;

; Draw scrolling scenery column using tile generator
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Handler for index $15 of the #R$A000 jump table (see #R$B7F6).
c$A445 LD HL,($9BAB) ; get Scenery data pointer
 $A448 LD A,($9BFF)  ;
 $A44B LD C,A        ;
*$A44C LD B,$09      ;
*$A44E CALL $A499    ; Generate next scenery/terrain cell value
 $A451 LD (HL),A     ;
 $A452 INC L         ;
 $A453 DJNZ $A44E    ;
 $A455 DEC C         ;
 $A456 JR Z,$A46B    ;
 $A458 LD A,L        ; {Wrap column offset back +8 rows for the descending pass
 $A459 ADD A,$08     ;
 $A45B LD L,A        ; }
 $A45C PUSH HL       ;
 $A45D LD B,$09      ;
*$A45F CALL $A499    ; Generate next scenery/terrain cell value
 $A462 LD (HL),A     ;
 $A463 DEC L         ;
 $A464 DJNZ $A45F    ;
 $A466 POP HL        ;
 $A467 INC L         ;
 $A468 DEC C         ;
 $A469 JR NZ,$A44C   ;
*$A46B RET           ;

; Draw scrolling scenery column (variant, using tile generator)
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Handler for index $16 of the #R$A000 jump table (see #R$B7F6).
; .
; Structurally similar to #R$A445 (same #R$A499 tile-generator calls building a
; column into HL) but with a +9 row stride and 5-row outer loop instead of
; #R$A445's layout - likely a different scenery band/type sharing the same
; generator.
c$A46C LD HL,($9BAB) ; {HL = source pointer; C = pass count; E = 5 (outer loop
 $A46F LD A,($9BFF)  ; count)
 $A472 LD C,A        ;
 $A473 LD E,$05      ; }
*$A475 LD B,C        ;
 $A476 LD A,L        ;
*$A477 CALL $A499    ; Generate next scenery/terrain cell value
 $A47A LD (HL),A     ; {Store cell, advance column by +9, loop
 $A47B LD A,L        ;
 $A47C ADD A,$09     ;
 $A47E LD L,A        ;
 $A47F DJNZ $A477    ; }
 $A481 SUB $08       ; {Wrap column back -8 for the descending pass
 $A483 LD L,A        ;
 $A484 DEC E         ;
 $A485 JR Z,$A498    ; }
 $A487 LD B,C        ;
 $A488 LD A,L        ;
*$A489 CALL $A499    ; Generate next scenery/terrain cell value
 $A48C LD (HL),A     ; {Store cell, advance column by -9, loop
 $A48D LD A,L        ;
 $A48E SUB $09       ;
 $A490 LD L,A        ;
 $A491 DJNZ $A489    ; }
 $A493 ADD A,$0A     ; {Wrap column back +10, loop the outer pass
 $A495 LD L,A        ;
 $A496 JR $A475      ; }
*$A498 RET           ;

; Generate next scenery/terrain cell value
;
; Used by the routines at #R$A445 and #R$A46C.
;
; O:A generated cell value (base $9C0B + next script nibble)
;   HL preserved
;
; Generates the next terrain cell value, periodically refreshing its base value
; from the scenery data.
c$A499 PUSH HL       ;
 $A49A LD HL,$9C0A   ; {Refresh counter ($9C0A) hit zero? refresh base value
 $A49D LD A,(HL)     ; below
 $A49E AND A         ;
 $A49F JR NZ,$A4AB   ; }
 $A4A1 CALL $A4B5    ; Read next byte (2 nibbles) from scenery-event data
 $A4A4 LD ($9C0B),A  ;
 $A4A7 CALL $A4B5    ; Read next byte (2 nibbles) from scenery-event data
 $A4AA LD (HL),A     ;
*$A4AB DEC (HL)      ; Otherwise just count down to the next refresh
 $A4AC CALL $A4C4    ; Extract next 4-bit parameter from scenery-event data
 $A4AF LD HL,$9C0B   ;
 $A4B2 ADD A,(HL)    ;
 $A4B3 POP HL        ;
 $A4B4 RET           ;

; Read next byte (2 nibbles) from scenery-event data
;
; Used by the routine at #R$A499.
;
; .
;
; Combines two calls to #R$A4C4 (high nibble then low nibble) into a full byte.
; Corrects an earlier guess at #R$A499 - this is just a byte reader, not a PRNG
; source.
c$A4B5 PUSH BC       ;
 $A4B6 CALL $A4C4    ; Extract next 4-bit parameter from scenery-event data
 $A4B9 ADD A,A       ;
 $A4BA ADD A,A       ;
 $A4BB ADD A,A       ;
 $A4BC ADD A,A       ;
 $A4BD LD C,A        ;
 $A4BE CALL $A4C4    ; Extract next 4-bit parameter from scenery-event data
 $A4C1 OR C          ;
 $A4C2 POP BC        ;
 $A4C3 RET           ;

; Extract next 4-bit parameter from scenery-event data
;
; Used by the routines at #R$A3A0, #R$A499 and #R$A4B5.
;
; O:A the extracted nibble (0-15)
;
; Unpacks the next 4-bit parameter from the scenery-event data, alternating
; between a byte's high and low nibble on successive calls.
c$A4C4 PUSH HL       ;
 $A4C5 PUSH BC       ;
 $A4C6 LD HL,($9C0C) ; HL = current byte pointer ($9C0C)
 $A4C9 LD A,($9C0E)  ;
 $A4CC AND (HL)      ; {Mask out the selected nibble
 $A4CD LD C,A        ; }
 $A4CE LD A,($9C0E)  ;
 $A4D1 CPL           ; {Flip nibble-select mask ($9C0E); test which nibble just
 $A4D2 LD ($9C0E),A  ; finished
 $A4D5 CP $F0        ; }
 $A4D7 LD A,C        ;
 $A4D8 JR NZ,$A4E0   ; Skip shift if this was the low-nibble read
 $A4DA INC HL        ; {Advance byte pointer (low nibble just consumed) and
 $A4DB LD ($9C0C),HL ; return
 $A4DE JR $A4E4      ; }
*$A4E0 RRCA          ; {Shift high nibble down to low bits
 $A4E1 RRCA          ;
 $A4E2 RRCA          ;
 $A4E3 RRCA          ; }
*$A4E4 POP BC        ;
 $A4E5 POP HL        ;
 $A4E6 RET           ;

; Find level index from formation tag, reset state, select colour scheme
;
; Used by the routine at #R$A612.
;
; .
;
; Finds which level a wave belongs to, resets scenery/event state for it, and
; selects that level's colour scheme.
@label=select_level_colour
c$A4E7 LD IX,($9C77) ; {IX = current object's data; set a status flag
 $A4EB LD HL,$9BA2   ;
 $A4EE SET 5,(HL)    ;
 $A4F0 PUSH HL       ; }
 $A4F1 LD HL,($9BA7) ; {Point at 8-entry threshold table; B=8, A=wave's tag
 $A4F4 LD A,(IX+$07) ; (IX+$07)
 $A4F7 LD B,$08      ; }
*$A4F9 CP (HL)       ; {Search for the first entry >= the wave's tag
 $A4FA JR Z,$A502    ;
 $A4FC JR C,$A501    ;
 $A4FE INC HL        ;
 $A4FF DJNZ $A4F9    ;
*$A501 DEC HL        ; }
*$A502 LD A,(HL)     ;
 $A503 LD ($9BA4),A  ; set Level progress / index
 $A506 CALL $A371    ; Reset various state pointers/counters to defaults
 $A509 LD A,($9BA4)  ; get Level progress / index
 $A50C LD L,A        ; {Level index * 16 + $D0 -> starting scroll offset
 $A50D LD H,$00      ;
 $A50F ADD HL,HL     ;
 $A510 ADD HL,HL     ;
 $A511 ADD HL,HL     ;
 $A512 ADD HL,HL     ;
 $A513 LD DE,$00D0   ;
 $A516 ADD HL,DE     ; }
*$A517 PUSH HL       ;
 $A518 CALL $A3A0    ; Scenery/event script interpreter
 $A51B CALL $C8B8    ; Advance background scroll
 $A51E POP HL        ; {Decrement offset, loop until column exhausted
 $A51F DEC HL        ;
 $A520 LD A,L        ;
 $A521 OR H          ;
 $A522 JR NZ,$A517   ; }
 $A524 LD HL,($9BA5) ; get Timeline table cursor
 $A527 LD A,($9BA4)  ; get Level progress / index
 $A52A LD DE,$0003   ; {DE = 3 (table stride)
 $A52D AND A         ; }
 $A52E SBC HL,DE     ;
*$A530 ADD HL,DE     ; {Advance cursor until entry covers the level index
 $A531 CP (HL)       ;
 $A532 JR NC,$A530   ; }
 $A534 LD ($9BA5),HL ; set Timeline table cursor
 $A537 LD A,$07      ; {Init a couple of timer/event fields for the new level
 $A539 LD ($9BA3),A  ;
 $A53C LD HL,$9C47   ;
 $A53F LD ($9C45),HL ;
 $A542 LD A,$02      ;
 $A544 LD ($9C44),A  ;
 $A547 LD HL,($9C57) ; }
 $A54A LD A,($9BA4)  ; get Level progress / index
*$A54D CP (HL)       ; {Scan colour-scheme table until the level's threshold
 $A54E INC HL        ; entry
 $A54F INC HL        ;
 $A550 JR C,$A54D    ; }
 $A552 LD ($9C57),HL ;
 $A555 DEC HL        ; {Step back to the entry, read its colour/type value
 $A556 LD A,(HL)     ; }
 $A557 LD ($9C59),A  ; set Active colour scheme
 $A55A LD ($9C5A),A  ;
 $A55D POP HL        ;
 $A55E RES 5,(HL)    ;
 $A560 RET           ;

; Player respawn/continue state check
;
; Used by the routine at #R$A0C4.
;
; .
;
; Runs the death/recovery timer, or if it's disabled, polls ENTER for a manual
; continue, then dispatches the player's next state.
@label=respawn_check
c$A561 LD HL,$9C3C   ; {Death/recovery timer ($9C3C); count down, A=4 on expiry
 $A564 LD A,(HL)     ;
 $A565 CP $FF        ;
 $A567 JR Z,$A570    ;
 $A569 DEC (HL)      ;
 $A56A JR NZ,$A570   ;
 $A56C LD A,$04      ;
 $A56E JR $A57C      ; }
*$A570 LD A,$F7      ; {Timer disabled: poll ENTER key, A=0 if held else A=2
 $A572 IN A,($FE)    ;
 $A574 BIT 3,A       ;
 $A576 LD A,$00      ;
 $A578 JR NZ,$A57C   ;
 $A57A LD A,$02      ; }
*$A57C CALL $A599    ; Ratchet player state forward
 $A57F LD A,($9C3D)  ;
 $A582 LD HL,$A038   ;
 $A585 CALL $B7F6    ; Jump-table dispatcher

; No-op state (index $1C)
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Handler for index $1C of the #R$A000 jump table (see #R$B7F6).
@label=noop_A588
c$A588 RET           ;

; Exit gameplay: mirror state, play alert sound, switch to light ISR
;
; .
;
; .
;
; Handler for indices $1F, $20 of the #R$A000 jump table (see #R$B7F6).
; .
; Takes the game out of active gameplay: confirms the player state, plays an
; alert sound, and switches back to the light per-frame handler.
c$A589 LD A,($9C3D)  ; Confirm the player state ($9C3D -> $9C3E)
 $A58C LD ($9C3E),A  ;
 $A58F CALL $A1CE    ; Request sound effect at maximum priority
 $A592 LD HL,$A0B0   ; point to per-frame handler #R$A0B0 (light ISR)
 $A595 LD ($FDFE),HL ; set ISR handler address
 $A598 RET           ;

; Ratchet player state forward (only increase, never decrease)
;
; Used by the routines at #R$A561 and #R$BE4A.
;
; A candidate new state value
;
; Updates $9C3D (the state #R$A561/$A57F reads for its dispatch) only if A is
; >= the current value; otherwise leaves it unchanged. Ensures the
; respawn/continue state only ever advances.
c$A599 LD HL,$9C3D   ;
 $A59C CP (HL)       ;
 $A59D RET C         ;
 $A59E LD (HL),A     ;
 $A59F RET           ;

; Starts music track 0.
@label=music_start_0
c$A5A0 XOR A         ;
 $A5A1 CALL $A927    ; Start playing music track A
 $A5A4 RET           ;

; Show title screen once, then (re)initialize interrupts
;
; Used by the routine at #R$A8C0.
;
; .
;
; Draws the title screen once (on first call), then (re)builds the graphics
; tables and points the ISR back at the light per-frame handler.
c$A5A5 DI            ; {"Shown once" flag ($9B9F); skip drawing if already set
 $A5A6 LD HL,$9B9F   ;

 $A5AB CP (HL)       ;
 $A5AC LD (HL),A     ;
 $A5AD JR Z,$A5B8    ; }
